stories.title: Isaiah Joe scores 22 points, Pistons' reserves power NBA Cup win over Bucks
stories.summary: — Isaiah Joe scored 22 points to help the Detroit Pistons overcome a slow start and beat the Milwaukee Bucks 113-98 in an NBA Cup game Friday night.
stories.detailText: DETROIT -- — Isaiah Joe scored 22 points to help the Detroit Pistons overcome a slow start and beat the Milwaukee Bucks 113-98 in an NBA Cup game Friday night. The Pistons wpn East Group A at 3-1 with a better points differential than the Toronto Raptors and Orlando Magic . Detroit will host a knockout-round game and could finish with the Eastern Conference's top seed. The Bucks finished 0-4 in group play. The Pistons, who finished with seven players in double figures, were missing three starters — Jalen Duren (hamstring) and Duncan Robinson (quadriceps) have been out for weeks, and Cade Cunningham (knee) also was in street clothes. Paul Reed and fellow reserve Elijah Harkless added 14 points. Detroit had 60 bench points while the starters finished with 53. Rookie Brayden Burries had 23 points for the Bucks and Tyler Herro added 20. Milwaukee led by 16 points in the first quarter, but only had a two-point advantage at halftime. The Pistons then put up a 42-point third quarter that included points from eight players. Daniss Jenkins ' 3-pointer at the buzzer put Detroit up 90-78 at quarter's end. Officials and coaches had to jump in between the players midway through the fourth after Myles Turner fired a ball into Ausar Thompson 's back. Both players were given technical fouls. After the confrontation, the game turned into a dunk fest for the Pistons, who got points from nine players in an 64-point second half. The Bucks had a rare good start, taking a 19-3 lead before Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff pulled all of his starters. The reserves got Detroit back into the game, then went on a 15-2 run to take the lead in the second quarter. Milwaukee led 50-48 at halftime, with Detroit's starters only contributing 12 points. Up next Bucks: Host Oklahoma City on Saturday night. Pistons: Host Orlando on Sunday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.title: Antetokounmpo has 22 points and 23 rebounds as the Heat stop the Knicks' 6-game winning streak
stories.summary: — Giannis Antetokounmpo had 22 points and a career-high 23 rebounds, Bam Adebayo scored 25 points and the Miami Heat ended the New York Knicks' six-game winning streak and NBA Cup title reign with a 108-105 victory Friday night.
stories.detailText: NEW YORK -- — Giannis Antetokounmpo had 22 points and a career-high 23 rebounds, Bam Adebayo scored 25 points and the Miami Heat ended the New York Knicks ' six-game winning streak and NBA Cup title reign with a 108-105 victory Friday night. The Knicks erased a 23-point deficit to grab the lead in the fourth quarter, but Jalen Brunson hit only two of three free throws when he was fouled shooting a 3-pointer with 9.8 seconds remaining and the Heat held on. Miami would win its group if Philadelphia lost in Indiana, but the 76ers had a huge lead in the fourth quarter. Brunson had 27 points and eight assists for the Knicks, who needed to win by at least seven points and have the 76ers lose to have a chance to become the first team to advance to the knockout round of the tournament with a 2-2 record. Karl-Anthony Towns had 19 points and 10 rebounds while playing with an abdominal injury that had him listed as questionable until shortly before the game and wincing in pain a few times during it. The Heat went 6 for 11 on 3s and the Knicks were 2 for 11 in the first quarter as Miami led 31-21. Towns got the first two baskets of the second before the Heat ran off 15 straight points for a 46-25 advantage. It was 58-35 after Adebayo's basket with 2:06 remaining, but the Knicks gained a little ground while Antetokounmpo was on the bench with three fouls and cut it to 60-44 at halftime. The Knicks got back in it with a 9-0 run early in the third quarter and went ahead 92-91 midway through the fourth. Adebayo's basket snapped a 95-all tie with 4:02 to play and the Heat stayed ahead from there. Up next Heat: Visit Cleveland on Sunday. Knicks: Host Atlanta on Sunday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.title: 3 Observations from Indiana men’s basketball’s 93-57 win over Bowling Green
stories.summary: Indiana men’s basketball cruised to a big win over Bowling Green to move to 8-0 on the season.
stories.detailText: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 9: Darian DeVries, head coach of the Indiana Hoosiers coaches during the game against the Syracuse Orange at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on November 9, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Indiana men’s basketball dominated Bowling Green tonight, going on a run just over five minutes into the game that effectively put the Falcons to bed. The Hoosiers were shooting well, defending well, and rebounding well in what may have been the most complete performance from this group so far. Though it wasn’t a marquee win like last week’s victories over Arkansas or Kentucky, the margin of victory was one that boosted Indiana’s computer profile. KenPom only favored Indiana by 20 entering the game, so the blowout moved Indiana up five spots in the national ranking. At 8-0, Indiana looks much improved over Darian DeVries’ first season, with KenPom now projecting the Hoosiers to win 23 games and go 12-8 in Big Ten play. Here are 3 Observations from the win: Ball Movement Indiana had a season-high 18 assists tonight against Bowling Green, starting to resemble the fast-paced offense we saw from DeVries’ group last year. While Indiana has more players that are capable of creating unassisted buckets, the ball movement tonight helped the Hoosiers take more quality looks from the perimeter, something that will be important for maintaining a respectable 3-point percentage this season. Bryce Lindsay’s deep shot against Arkansas will go down as a high-point of the season, but over the last couple games Indiana had gotten into the habit of chucking a few too many heat checks from deep or taking transition threes that negate the team’s rebounding advantage. Seeing the way the ball moved tonight was an encouraging step for this group not just cause it made the offense look a little better, but because it reflects well on the team’s chemistry so early in the season. With a team full of transfers, having nine different players record an assist in a game is no small feat. Aiden Sherrell Aiden Sherrell had one of his stronger performances of the season, finishing with 16 points, nine rebounds, two blocks and an assist. He also went 2-6 from 3-point range. Tonight’s performance was a good example of why he’s a potential NBA player. A seven footer who can score from the perimeter, rebound on both ends of the floor, and protect the rim is a valuable piece for any team. After an impressive year last year at Bama, he’s averaging more points and shooting better from deep this year at Indiana. Even though he cooled off by the end of the night, his early threes are exactly what Indiana will need from him going forward. Establishing himself as a threat at the beginning of the game will force defenses to account for him until the final whistle. Bryce Lindsay It’s hard to say enough good things about Bryce Lindsay so far this year. Against Bowling Green, he scored 18 points, grabbed five rebounds, had three assists, and also added two steals. He was also super efficient, going 2/4 from 3-point range and making all of his free throws. What I like most about Lindsay’s game is his ability to be what DeVries needs on the floor, no matter who he’s playing with. He can play point guard alongside Darren Harris at the shooting guard spot, or play shooting guard next to Markus Burton. Calling him the sixth man doesn’t even feel right, as he plays the fifth most minutes on the team, but he’s been a huge asset for DeVries and Indiana this year, doing everything asked of him, and then some.

stories.title: Golden State Warriors rule Steph Curry out for next 3 games with oblique injury
stories.summary: Golden State ruled Steph Curry out for the next three games, extending his absence for a torn oblique suffered earlier this month, saying he is making progress.
stories.detailText: The Golden State Warriors have ruled injured guard Steph Curry out for the next three games, extending his absence for a torn oblique suffered earlier this month. In a release, the Warriors said Curry is making progress and advancing to individual court work. He will be evaluated again Wednesday after the Warriors face the Utah Jazz on Tuesday night. Curry remained in San Francisco to work with Rick Celebrini, the team's lead medical decision-maker, while the team flew to Portland for a Friday night game against the Blazers . Curry will also miss Sunday's home game against the LA Clippers . Curry tore an oblique in the first quarter of a Nov. 11 road loss to the Houston Rockets . The Warriors entered that night on an eight-game winning streak, boasting an 8-3 record, but stumbled to an 0-5 road trip without Curry. In recent days, they have responded with two home wins over the Boston Celtics and Sacramento Kings to temporarily tread water without Curry, whom they have been expecting to miss around a month with the injury. Curry is averaging a scorching 27.8 points in 26.3 minutes in the 10 games he has appeared, making 50% of his shots, 45.7% of his 3s and missing only one of his 76 free throw attempts.

stories.detailText: Stephen Curry will miss at least three more games for the Golden State Warriors with an oblique tear. He will have the injury re-evaluated next week, the team announced on Friday . Curry, 38, has missed the Warriors' past six games with the abdominal injury, At the time, the Warriors announced that their star guard would be sidelined for at least two weeks before being re-evaluated . So this latest update approximately follows that timeline. The two-time NBA MVP has begun individual on-court workouts and is making good progress based on Friday's evaluation, according to the Warriors' release ( via the San Francisco Chronicle's Luca Evans ). #Warriors star Stephen Curry will be re-evaluated next Wednesday amid recovery from torn oblique, team says. Team says he is “making… pic.twitter.com/XSpvQeREoj — Luca Evans (@bylucaevans) November 28, 2026 Curry sustained the injury during the first quarter of Nov. 11's 115-108 loss to the Houston Rockets . After hitting a 3-pointer, he began reaching for his side. Curry's frustration seemed to indicate that he knew he was injured, though no contact was made with him on the play. He did not come out of the game immediately, but left midway through the quarter . Following the game, Warriors coach Steve Kerr told reporters that Curry had tweaked something in his abdominal area and "had never done it before." In 10 games this season, Curry is averaging 27.8 points, 3.7 rebounds and 3.9 assists. He's shooting 46% on 94 3-point attempts. If he maintains that scoring average, it would be his highest in the past four seasons. In his absence, the Warriors have gone 2-4, giving them a 10-8 record going into Friday's NBA Cup matchup with the Portland Trail Blazers (12-6). Golden State is 2-1 in the Western Conference's Group C play and would be eliminated from the in-season tournament with a loss. Following Friday's game, the Warriors host the Los Angeles Clippers (4-13) on Sunday and the Utah Jazz (3-16) on Tuesday. Curry will be re-evaluated the next day.

stories.title: Lakers forward has ‘a lot of special things’ planned being back in LA
stories.summary: Ziaire Williams is no stranger to giving back to the community that raised him.
stories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO — Ziaire Williams is no stranger to giving back to the community that raised him . The Lakers forward has hosted a free annual youth basketball camp in his hometown of Lancaster the last five years. Ziaire Williams takes pride in giving back to the local community. NBAE via Getty Images He once again hosted a Thanksgiving community event at Inglewood High last week for about 150 kids from the Boys & Girls Clubs of Metro Los Angeles, which he’s done every year since being the No. 10 pick in the 2021 NBA Draft. But the community events have landed differently for Williams since joining the Lakers as a free agent this past summer . Ziaire Williams shoots a 3-point basket. NBAE via Getty Images “I’ve been talking with my guy Mike, who does my foundation stuff; we got a lot of special things [planned],” Williams said after the Lakers’ shootaround Friday afternoon ahead of the game against the Spurs. “Definitely want to take advantage of this time while I can. I love the kids, love helping the kids. It’s nothing like seeing smiling faces. So that’s the first of many events that’ll be taking place back home.” After starting his NBA career with the Grizzlies (2021-24) and playing for the Nets (2024-26), Williams is looking to take advantage of the opportunities that’ll come with being closer to home. “I don’t want to share it yet until they’re official,” he said, “but, yeah, we got some nice little Christmas giveaways, some school stuff, a lot of good things at work, for sure.” Another perk of being back in Southern California for Williams was that he was able to spend time with family leading into Thanksgiving before the Lakers started their four-game road trip against the Spurs. The Lakers will also play the Grizzlies, Rockets and Pelicans as part of the trip. “Luckily for me, I’m from LA, so I was able to get a little early Thanksgiving Eve dinner,” Williams said. “Shoutout to my chef. I ain’t get grandma’s cooking back home, but I’m grateful I was able to see my fam the day before Thanksgiving.”

The Oklahoma City Thunder are at a critical inflection point. After winning a championship in 2024, they spent most of last season as the title favorites, only to be upended by Victor Wembanyama 's San Antonio Spurs in Game 7 of the Western Conference finals . Coming into the season, ESPN's Basketball Power Index (BPI) projected them to have a 28.4% chance to win the title, the highest of any team. However, several injuries have already derailed their season, leaving them in the middle of a crowded Western Conference at 10-8 and with a decision to make on which direction to take for the rest of the season. Some people are calling for Oklahoma City to punt on the season and regroup in 2027-28. With an All-Star in Jalen Williams and an All-Defensive player in Cason Wallace out of the lineup, is it worth using valuable draft capital to attempt to salvage what could turn into a lost season? Other people are adamant that now is the time for the Thunder to make an aggressive trade, dipping into their treasure trove of draft assets so they don't squander a year of reigning back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 's prime. The challenge for the Thunder in making a trade, however, is their growing cap sheet and current roster construction. With max extensions for their young core of Gilgeous-Alexander, Williams and Chet Holmgren on the books, they are just $3 million below the dreaded second apron . Beyond those three, the only other players on the team earning above $8 million annually are Alex Caruso and Isaiah Hartenstein , both of whom are invaluable to the Thunder's identity. This makes it difficult to include Caruso or Hartenstein in trades that would actually improve their championship hopes for this season. The remaining 10 players on their roster are all on extremely team-friendly deals, which actually works against the Thunder for the sake of facilitating a trade. Many of these young players would field significant value across the league, but their low salaries make it tough to aggregate outgoing money to match the paycheck of a veteran who could meaningfully improve OKC. Out of that group, Nikola Topic and Thomas Sorber might be the most logical trade candidates. They have been the two most-traded Thunder players in ESPN's NBA Trade Lab , after a series of injuries have kept them off the floor for the majority of their young careers. The Thunder recently declined to pick up Topic's $7.4 million option for next season, making him an unrestricted free agent in 2027. Let's evaluate a couple of the top fan-created trades from our NBA Trade Lab involving these two players to see what the Thunder could realistically bring back to help them this season: Trade No. 1: OKC adds a talented defender Thunder get: Herb Jones New Orleans Pelicans get: Sorber, Topic, one first-round pick Oklahoma City led the NBA in defensive turnover Net Points in each of the previous three seasons, but it has slipped to league-average this season. The Thunder's identity hinges on creating havoc and extra possessions, and without several key stoppers, they suddenly are much less intimidating in this area. Bringing in Jones, an all-defense-caliber wing who has always created turnovers, could help to restore their defensive edge until the return of some of their key defensive personnel. Jones might not provide much on offense, but one of Gilgeous-Alexander's superpowers is his ability to captain an elite offense even in a weak surrounding offensive context, allowing the Thunder to pack lineups full of suffocating defenders and still be competent on offense. Trade No. 2: OKC deals for instant offense help Thunder get: Ty Jerome and Olivier-Maxence Prosper Memphis Grizzlies get: Sorber, Topic, two first-round picks Jerome has been a breakout star for the Grizzlies, thriving in an expanded role as their primary creator while still maintaining his elite shotmaking, especially with his floater in the midrange. Net Points rated Jerome as one of the league's most impactful players since his 2023-24 season with the Cleveland Cavaliers , and now that he has been given a featured role on an upstart Memphis team, his talent has become clear. Jerome holds a $9 million player option for next season, and the Grizzlies can re-sign him to only a four-year, $72 million deal with his Bird rights, which is arguably below what his contract value would be on the open market. This leaves Memphis in a difficult position with Jerome potentially headed toward unrestricted free agency in 2027. Trading him now for two young players and two first-round picks might be a better option than risking him leaving for nothing in the summer. The challenge with this trade is the Thunder would also be limited in their ability to re-sign Jerome in the summer, given their current cap constraints and proximity to the second apron. If Jerome fits well alongside Gilgeous-Alexander and OKC decides to re-sign him long term, the team would likely need to trade one of its higher-paid foundational players to make room. -- Ben Tiemeyer Have any more ideas on moves the Thunder should make? At the time, Murray was viewed as a burgeoning young star with a strong impact on both sides of the ball. In 2024, the Hawks sent him to the Pelicans in exchange for a package that included two first-round picks and Dyson Daniels , who went on to win Most Improved Player the following season . Now in 2026, it appears likely Murray will be on the move again, but his market is difficult to read. His impact metrics have been on the decline, and he's making over $30 million for the next two seasons after turning 30 years old. At the same time, he is undoubtedly a talented player who could certainly find a renaissance in the right situation. He is also only 24, the same age as Warriors Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg , so the Pelicans could see room to further develop him in their system. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season. "I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit. "In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania . Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move. Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists. SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season. "No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row. "We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward." ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama , Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic . No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title: "It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is." Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures" Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year" During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season. "The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder." Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers . The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right." Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer. For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer. For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key. There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract. "I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do." Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons" At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense." "I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said. After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal. Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset. "This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win. "We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander , who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort , Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon. "It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit. "My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood." As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram 's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season. Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year" Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day. "I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me." Curry said knee is ready to go for the season Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee. "Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with." Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions. Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise Members of the Denver Nuggets ' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic 's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason. "We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns." LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title. "I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played. "I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it." James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20. No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr. 's contract. "I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that." The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason. Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant Portland Trail Blazers ' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday. "Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player. "I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent." Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant. Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton" Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season. "He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need. "Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks." Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season. Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey . "It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there." Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season. "I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said. Harper addresses role for coming season After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season. "Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in." First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team: "Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language." LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win. "Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything" Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings. "I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors." Haliburton: I am 100% healthy Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season. "I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year." Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team. In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors. Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room. "We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room." "I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control." And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done." Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday. Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft. Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday. Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said. Sept. 26 Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday. 2026 NBA offseason trade grades Sept. 25 What's next for Curry and the Warriors? Stephen Curry 's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings. The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer. By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million. For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer. Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski . The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury. James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July. "[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump." Grizzlies waive Russell The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.title: MRI on 76ers star Jaylen Brown's left hamstring showed no new injury
stories.summary: An MRI on Philadelphia 76ers forward Jaylen Brown's left hamstring revealed no aggravation or new injury, the Sixers announced Friday.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- An MRI on Philadelphia 76ers forward Jaylen Brown 's left hamstring revealed no aggravation or new injury, the Sixers announced Friday. Brown missed two games earlier this season because of a hamstring strain and had to exit the Sixers' most recent win over the Miami Heat because of the same injury. Brown is out for Friday's NBA Cup game against the Indiana Pacers and isn't with the team for this road trip, which will end with a game against the Houston Rockets on Saturday. 76ers coach Nick Nurse called it "good news" and a "positive sign" that Brown's MRI didn't show any injury, which was the Sixers' original concern. Center Joel Embiid , who has missed the past two games because of an illness, is questionable, and forward Dean Wade (hamstring) is out. After scoring his sixth point in Wednesday night's win over the Miami Heat on a step-back jump shot late in the second quarter, Brown immediately shook his head and grabbed his hamstring then signaled to the Sixers bench that he needed to check out of the game. The injury concern for Brown started in last week's win over the Brooklyn Nets , in which he tied his season high of 31 points. Brown left that game early because of a left hamstring strain and missed the Sixers' next two wins over the Orlando Magic and Milwaukee Bucks . He returned in Monday's loss to the Portland Trail Blazers , scoring 20 points. After that game, Brown said he had "a little bit of soreness." The earliest Brown could return is Dec. 1, when the Sixers play the Memphis Grizzlies . Brown is averaging 21.4 points, 6.0 rebounds and 3.4 assists this season. Friday's game is the final of NBA Cup group play. With a win, the 76ers will clinch Eastern Conference Group B and advance to the knockout rounds for the first time in franchise history.

stories.detailText: TORONTO, CANADA - NOVEMBER 23: Scottie Barnes #4 of the Toronto Raptors dribbles against Michael Porter Jr. #17 of the Brooklyn Nets during the second half at Scotiabank Arena on November 23, 2025 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. (Photo by Kevin Sousa/Getty Images) | Getty Images Some games are nice to win, other games are acceptable to lose, but giving up a victory to the Brooklyn Nets at this point would bring abject humiliation onto the Toronto Raptors fanbase. Last year, arguably the lowest point of the season was the Raptors’ loss to an even worse version of the Brooklyn Nets team in December of 2025. That game saw Michael Porter Jr. give the Raptors a lovely Christmas present of 24 points and 11 boards, outscoring 3 of the Raptors’ starters put together. The Nets won that game by 15 points. That was a dark day. The sun set at 4:00, the TTC was slow, and Scotiabank Arena was a place of despair rather than joy. The Raps need to avoid a repeat of that happening. TORONTO, CANADA – NOVEMBER 23: Scottie Barnes #4 of the Toronto Raptors dribbles against Michael Porter Jr. #17 of the Brooklyn Nets during the second half at Scotiabank Arena on November 23, 2025 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Kevin Sousa/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Nets are playing with both of their best players active, meaning that Toronto will be in for a challenge containing Porter Jr. and Julius Randle both. MPJ is a fantastic jump shooter whose height and accuracy makes him a deadly marksman that Allen Graves and Collin Murray-Boyles will be hard pressed to contain. Inversely, Julius Randle is one of the strongest, most physical players in the league, capable of bullying his way to easy points and rebounds. Scottie Barnes will likely take this defensive matchup, able to meet Randle in the paint more capably than perhaps anyone else in the league, short of Victor Wembanyama. Graves has seemingly earned more opportunities to prove himself, and will be starting in tonight’s matchup. The rookie has shown flashes of serious scoring and defensive ability, and on a night that would normally be a low-pressure matchup for the Raps, giving the rookie more opportunities and a greater defensive responsibility will go a long way to helping his development. Indeed, not only is tonight marked by a chance to pick up a much-needed win during a rough part of the season, but it’s an NBA Cup night, meaning that beyond the special courts, the Raptors have a chance to notch another win during the Group Stage of the former In-Season Tournament. Group Play in the Emirates NBA Cup 2026 concludes on Friday with 11 games. Here are the scenarios for Friday ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/dSZH8gvGKw — NBA Communications (@NBAPR) November 26, 2026 The NBA broke down what the Raptors would need to advance tonight. While a win tonight, coupled with the Detroit Pistons winning their matchup tonight, and then a Toronto tiebreaker win would clinch it for the Raptors, a few other scenarios involving a Toronto win, or a loss with a small point differential coupled with some good luck in other Cup games, could send the team forward. Moving onto the next stage of the Cup would give the Raptors a chance to play or something with smaller stakes, rebuild the team’s confidence in themselves, and the fans’ confidence in the team. Falling out this early with Avoiding insult being added to injury would be the optimal result of tonight’s game. Losing to the Nets last year was a blow to a team that were mere playoff hopefuls. This season, the Raptors have thus far failed to meet expectations, between some poor late-game performances and some serious starter injuries that have driven the Raptors to the point they find themselves at now.

stories.title: Former NBA lottery pick Rob Dillingham gets punched by Wizards rookie Felix Okpara during G League game
stories.summary: Okpara threw a punch at Dillingham after being shoved with no call from the officials. A melee then broke out among players from both G League teams.
stories.detailText: Playing for the G League Westchester Knicks, former NBA first-round pick Rob Dillingham was involved in a scuffle during Friday's matchup with the Capital City Go-Go. In the fourth quarter of Westchester's 125-104 win , Dillingham was punched by Capital City center Felix Okpara at the top of the 3-point line. Dillingham pushed Okpara on his way down the court, and the center looked at the official for a foul call. When one wasn't made, Okpara clotheslined Dillingham across the neck and shoulders, knocking him to the floor. Former lottery pick and now Westchester #Knicks PG Rob Dillingham punched by Capital City GoGo big man Felix Okpara Thankfully, Ermal Kuqo - the WestChester Knicks front office exec, who separated hot heads, is 6-10 and 270 lbs pic.twitter.com/wg1FbELQyq — Darko Dželetović (@DarkoBasketball) November 27, 2026 Both teams then gathered in a scrum past the Westchester basket, going off the court as Okpara backpedaled toward the baseline. Coaches, officials and arena security personnel then separated each group of players. Ermal Kuqo, the Knicks' senior director of minor league operations, and his 6-foot-10, 270-pound frame also got involved, which surely helped provide a significant obstacle to fisticuffs. Dillingham and Okpara were subsequently both ejected from the game. Dillingham finished with 10 points and 8 assists, while Okpara scored 12 points with 9 rebounds for the Go-Go. Okpara was the Washington Wizards' second-round pick in the 2026 NBA Draf t , selected No. 46 overall out of Tennessee. In three games with the Wizards, he averaged one point and 0.7 rebounds in five minutes of play. In the G League, Okpara is scoring 11.4 points, 8.8 rebounds and 2.4 blocks per game. Dillingham was the San Antonio Spurs' 2024 first-round pick, selected No. 8 overall out of Kentucky. He was traded to the Minnesota Timberwolves on draft night for a first-round pick swap in 2030 and first-rounder in 2031. Last season, the T-Wolves dealt him midway through his second season in a trade involving Ayo Dosunmu going to the Chicago Bulls . Before training camp this season, he was moved to the Charlotte Hornets in exchange for Buddy Hield but was subsequently waived. In November, he signed with the New York Knicks' G League team . In three games with Westchester, Dillingham is averaging 21 points and 6.3 assists per game while shooting 35% on 17 3-point attempts.

stories.title: Wizards rookie Felix Okpara punches Rob Dillingham in G League tilt
stories.summary: Wizards two-way forward Felix Okpara threw a punch at Westchester Knicks guard Rob Dillingham, sparking a brief fight during a G League game Friday night.
stories.detailText: A fight spilled into the sideline of a G League game on Friday afternoon after Washington Wizards rookie Felix Okpara threw a punch at former NBA lottery pick and current Westchester Knicks guard Rob Dillingham. With eight minutes to go in the fourth quarter, Westchester's Dillingham gave Okpara a shove after jogging past half court. Okpara responded by looking around for a foul call, and when that did not come, threw a punch that appeared to connect with the side of Dillingham's face. The punch caused Dillingham to fall to the ground, but he quickly got up and chased after a retreating Okpara before players and officials were able to break up the altercation. Okpara and Dillingham were both ejected from the game, a 125-104 win for Westchester. Dillingham, a former No. 8 pick in the 2024 NBA draft, was waived by the Charlotte Hornets in September and has spent the season in the G League. Okpara, 22, was selected in the second round of the 2026 draft and is on a two-way deal with the Wizards.

Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Melissa Majchrzak/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images It goes without saying that this Utah Jazz season has been a colossal disappointment for fans that were expecting a quick turnaround, after years of extraordinary tanking. At 3-16, the Utah Jazz have struggled out the gate, losing close game after close game and have been smacked straight in the mouth with injuries to key players Jaren Jackson Jr, Jusuf Nurkic, and Lauri Markkanen. While at times tough to watch, there are also glimpses of what this team can become. The Jazz are rarely blownout of the gym and frequently keep games close. But just as often, the youth on this team (namely Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson, and Ace Bailey) find themselves unable to finish off wins or comeback and steal wins. Many games have given fans brief moments of levity and whiffs of a win, only for that hope to be snatched away with Utah’s dumb turnovers, rookie mistakes, or just straight-up missed shots. There is also something to be said for the difficulty of Utah’s schedule thus far. This one will be a tough one. The Jazz lack size and will have to contend with former MVP Nikola Jokic. While a somewhat disappointing season relative to other years, the Denver Nuggets are still 10-6 and receiving All-Star caliber seasons from both Jamal Murray and Jokic. They struggle with their depth and have not received the best play from Christian Braun (on a crazy contract); Aaron Gordon as well looks to be a shell of himself, with years of injuries finally catching up to him. There is hope on the horizon. Word on the street is that Jusuf Nurkic is getting close to suiting up. As of this morning, he was listed as questionable. If Nurkic plays, it could end up being the most important moment in the season for this struggling team. The Heels are going into this one with just one loss on the season, while the Mountaineers have two losses, both of which were against ranked teams. This will likely be the Heels’ toughest test so far, but this is also a bit of a different team from the one that played Georgia. Having Cameron Fens in the lineup has made a difference, and one would argue that Terrence Brown playing point guard in Neo Avdalis’ absence has had more of a positive impact on the team than a negative. The thing, though, is his ability to be a facilitator will be tested big in a big way tonight. The Mountaineers are currently averaging 8 steals per game, which is slightly higher than what Carolina has been doing. Having a team that is that active on defense when you do not have your starting point guard can be tough, so we’ll see if Brown is able to take care of the ball. On the flip side, West Virginia is also averaging 9.8 turnovers per game, which funny enough is also somewhat similar to UNC’s numbers. This game will ultimately come down to who can take care of the ball better and who will be able to rebound, but of course neither matter if the ball isn’t going into the basket. Given how aggressive the Heels have been in the paint — mostly because of the crazy stuff Brown has been able to do — it’s hard to see scoring being the big issue tonight. stories.summary: The Celtics look to clinch the top seed in the NBA Emirates Cup with a win over the Hawks.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA, GA - MARCH 30: Jalen Johnson #1 of the Atlanta Hawks shoots the ball during the game against the Boston Celtics on March 30, 2026 at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, Georgia. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Joe Boatman/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Atlanta Hawks (11-6) at Boston Celtics (12-6) Friday, November 27, 2026 8:00 PM ET Regular Season Game #19, Home Game #8 TV: NBCSB, ANF/PSN/Prime Video, NBA-LP Radio: 98.5 Sports Hub, 92.9 The Game, Sirius XM TD Garden The Celtics return home from their 4 game road trip to take on the Atlanta Hawks. This is the first of 3 games between these teams this season. They will play 2 more games in Atlanta on February 15 and April 9. They split the series 2-2 last season with each team winning one at home and one on the road. The Celtics are 247-153 overall, all time against the Hawks. They are 133-46 in games played at Boston. This is the final NBA Emirates Cup group game for both teams. The Hawks are 2-1 and the Celtics are the only unbeaten team in the East in group play at 3-0. To make the quarterfinals for the first time since 2023, the Celtics need to beat Atlanta because head to head matchup would be the tie breaker should the Hawks win. They could make it into the quarterfinals as the wild card team if their point differential ends up the largest. Currently they have the best point differential at +68. Detroit +31, Miami +25, Cleveland +24 and Atlanta +21 could challenge that with a Celtics loss and a blow out win from any of those teams. The Celtics finally got a win after 4 straight losses and are now 2nd in the East, 2.5 games behind 1st place Philadelphia and they are tied with 3rd place New York and half a game ahead of 4th place Atlanta. They are 11-2 against Eastern Conference opponents. They are 6-1 at home and 6-4 in their last 10 games. They won their last game. The Hawks are 4th in the East, 3 games behind 1st place Philadelphia and half a game behind 2nd place Boston. They are 10-2 against Eastern Conference teams. They are 6-3 on the road and 8-2 in their last 10 games. They have won their last 4 games. The Hawks made some changes since last season. They brought in Lugentz Dort, Aaron Wiggins, Devin Carter and Ryan Nembhard through trades. They waived Carter and Nembhard before the season. They drafted Kingston Flemings with the 8th pick in the draft, Zuby Ejiofor with the 23rd pick and Henri Veesaar with the 52nd pick in the draft. They lost Zacharie Risacher, Gabe Vincent, Christian Koloko, Tony Bradley, and Keaton Wallace. After this game at home, the Celtics will be back on the road playing at San Antonio and Dallas. Then it’s home against Charlotte before the break for the NBA Cup tournament. Then, they play a game at Brooklyn before they have a 7 game home stand against Washington twice, Utah, Detroit, Portland, Miami and Cleveland. Then it’s back on the road for a 6 game road trip through Chicago, Utah, Portland, Phoenix, the LA Lakers and the LA Clippers. The Hawks are playing in the first game of a 3 game road trip that will take them to New York and Miami after this game. They then host Indiana before the break for the NBA Cup Tournament. Then they go on a 3 game road trip through Portland, Phoenix and Denver before they host Orlando, Oklahoma City, Detroit and Charlotte. Then they are back on the road to play one game at San Antonio before hosting Chicago, Milwaukee and Dallas. The Celtics have been rotating players at the shooting guard spot. They have started Jordan Walsh, Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman and most recently, Sam Hauser. The starting lineup of White, Hauser, George, Tatum and Queta are a plus-54 per 100 possessions and they got off to an 18-9 start en route to an 80 point first half. However, after the game, Joe Mazzulla was iffy about sticking with this lineup. I’m guessing that Hauser starts again, but he could go back to Walsh, Scheierman or Gonzalez. I’ve listed the Hawks starters from their game notes. Mitchell Robinson is the only player on the Celtics injury report at this time and he is once again out due to an illness. The Hawks have 5 players on the injury report. Mouhamed Gueye is out after surgery to repair a fractured left foot. Jock Landale is out due to a hip injury. CJ McCollum is out with a left calf strain. Asa Newell is out after undergoing surgery to repair a plantar plate tear in his left great toe. Henri Veesaar is out or the season due to a torn ACL. Probable Starting Matchups PG: Derrick White vs Kingston Flemings Derrick White | Getty Images Kingston Flemings | NBAE via Getty Images SG: Sam Hauser vs Nickeil Alexander-Walker Sam Hauser | Getty Images Nickeil Alexander-Walker | Getty Images SF: Paul George vs Dyson Daniels Paul George | NBAE via Getty Images Dyson Daniels | NBAE via Getty Images PF: Jayson Tatum vs Jalen Johnson Jayson Tatum | NBAE via Getty Images Jalen Johnson | NBAE via Getty Images C: Neemias Queta vs Onyeka Okongwu Neemias Queta | NBAE via Getty Images Onyeka Okongwu | Getty Images Celtics Reserves Chris Cenac, Jr Mike Conley, Jr Luka Garza Jordan Walsh Ron Harper, Jr Hugo Gonzalez Payton Pritchard Baylor Scheierman Two Way Players Devin Carter Dillon Mitchell Amari Williams Injuries/Out Mitchell Robinson (illness) out Head Coach Joe Mazzulla Hawks Reserves Lugentz Dort Zuby Ejiofor Dorian Finney-Smith Corey Kispert Aaron Wiggins 2-Way Players Rafael Castro RayJ Dennis Jalen Wilson Injured/Out Mouhamed Gueye (foot) out CJ McCollum (calf) out Henri Veesaar (knee) out Asa Newell (toe) out Jock Landale (hip) out Head Coach Quin Snyder Key Matchups Sam Hauser vs Nickeil Alexander-Walker Alexander-Walker is averaging 21.3 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.9 assists, and 1.3 steals per game. He is shooting 41.4% from the field and 35.9% from beyond the arc. He is a good 3 point shooter and so the Celtics need to defend him on the perimeter but they also need to keep him out of the paint. Joe may go with defense and start Walsh or Gonzalez here to defend Alexander-Walker. Jayson Tatum vs Jalen Johnson Johnson is averaging 19.1 points, 9.1 rebounds, 6.9 assists and 1.1 steals per game. He is shooting 44.7% from the field and 21.1% from beyond the arc. Even though he is not shooting 3’s well, the Celtics still need to cover him on the perimeter. They also need to keep him off the boards as he is a good rebounder. Hopefully Tatum can pick up where he left off against the Wizards. Honorable Mention Neemias Queta vs Onyeka Okongwu Okongwu is averaging 14.5 points, 8.2 rebounds and 2.4 assists per game while shooting 42.9% from the field and 33.3% from beyond the arc. The Celtics need to keep him out of the paint and off the boards, but they can’t leave him open on the perimeter because he is capable of hitting 3’s. Keys to the Game Defense – Defense is always a key to winning games. The Celtics have an offensive rating of 115.7 (9th) while the Hawks have an offensive rating of 112.7, which is 20th. The Celtics have a defensive rating of 105.8 which is 2nd while the Hawks have a defensive rating of 109.7, which is 6th. The Celtics have been hot and cold on defense this season. Most of the time they can shut down the other team but sometimes they allow them to score at will like allowing the Magic to score 40 in the 4th quarter or the lowly Kings to score 35 in the 3rd quarter. The Celtics need to defend the perimeter because the Hawks are 4th, shooting 43.3 threes a game. They also have to defend the paint as the Hawks are 6th with 51.2 points in the paint per game. The Celtics must make defense a priority in this game and they have to play that tough defense for 48 minutes and not let up. Rebound – Next to defense, rebounding is the key to winning. When the Celtics put out the extra effort on the boards, it usually carries through to the rest of their game. The Hawks are averaging 45.7 rebounds per game (5th) while the Celtics are averaging 45.2 rebounds per game (10th). The Celtics need to aggressively go after every rebound. They can’t afford to give the Hawks extra possessions and 2nd chance points by allowing them to beat them to rebounds. The Hawks are 5th with 16.9 second chance points per game and so the Celtics must keep them off the offensive glass. Effort and Focus for 48 Minutes – The Celtics have to play with extra effort overall for all 4 quarters. In most of their losses and even in some of their wins, they have allowed their opponents to play with more energy than them for periods of time during the game. They play well for stretches but let up and allow their opponents to surge ahead, especially in the 3rd quarter. The Celtics offensive rating in the 3rd quarter is 96.9 and their defensive rating in the 3rd quarter is 124.8, giving them a net rating of -27.9, which is the 2nd worst in the league. They have to stay focused for all 48 minutes and be ready for their opponents to play harder in the second half and they need to match that effort. They also have to come out with more effort and energy to start the game and not dig themselves into a hole. The Hawks have been playing very well and so the Celtics will need maximum effort for all 48 minutes to beat them. Move the Ball Carefully – When the Celtics move the ball and find the open man, they are tough to beat. When they hold the ball and try to do too much individually, they become predictable and struggle. The Hawks move the ball well and average 30.3 assists per game while the Celtics are 16th with 26.7 assists per game. The Celtics need to move the ball, but they have to make careful passes because the Hawks are 2nd in the league with 22.6 points off turnovers per game. X-Factors Home Game and Cup Game – They call it home court advantage for a reason and the Celtics need to take advantage of playing on their home court. The Celtics need to get motivation from the home crowd, which should be loud and doing everything in their power to support the Celtics and rattle the Hawks. However, it is the first game at home after a long road trip and those games are tough on the home team. The Hawks have the distractions of travel, an unfamiliar arena and a hostile crowd and hopefully that will give the Celtics an advantage. The Hawks have been off since Sunday and so may also have some rust to deal with. Both teams should have extra motivation to win this game in order to advance to the quarterfinals of the NBA Cup. Officiating – Officiating is always an x-factor in every game. Every crew officiates differently. Some call it tight, others let them play. The Celtics need to adjust to how the refs are calling the game and not allow bad calls or no calls to take away their focus from playing the game the right way. We have seen how much of an x-factor officiating can be in a few games this season. The Celtics have to play so well all game that the officiating, no matter how bad, can’t influence the outcome.

stories.title: Lakers must be aggressive, plug biggest hole that could sink title chances
stories.summary: Rob Pelinka knows he needs to go all in. The Lakers are championship contenders. Luka Doncic is leading the MVP race. If the GM plays his cards right, his team...
stories.detailText: Rob Pelinka knows he needs to go all in. The Lakers are championship contenders . Luka Doncic is leading the MVP race . If the GM plays his cards right, his team could be in a position to hang its 18th banner. But first, the Lakers need to address a glaring hole. Brook Lopez #11 of the LA Clippers and Isaiah Stewart #28 of the Memphis Grizzlies battle for the ball on Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026, in Memphis, Tenn. Getty Images They need a backup center. They’re dangerously thin at that position, an issue that could be a fatal flaw in a playoff series. You know who could be an intriguing option? Brook Lopez. The Clippers are sellers. They’re open for business. Their players could be dealt at bargain rates. With Kawhi Leonard, James Harden and Ivica Zubac gone, and the Clippers ravaged by the fallout from the Aspiration scandal , including losing five future first-round draft picks, the team is in full rebuild mode with the goal of trying to get draft assets. That means Lopez could be prime for the picking. The 7-foot-1 Lopez won a championship with the Bucks in 2021. He’s averaging 14.4 points (55% shooting from the field, 43.3% from beyond the arc), 5.1 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game for the Clippers this season. He’d give the Lakers a great option behind Walker Kessler. He’s a strong rim protector. His efficient outside shooting could especially be an asset against someone like Victor Wembanyama, helping draw him out of the paint. The downside? Lopez is 38. The Lakers may want to acquire a younger center who could be a mainstay on the roster alongside Doncic, Kessler and Austin Reaves in the future. And Lopez’s defensive mobility leaves a bit to be desired when compared with younger, more athletic bigs. But the Lakers are in win-now mode, and Lopez could undoubtedly help tip them over the edge this season. Brook Lopez of the LA Clippers drives to the basket against the Memphis Grizzlies in Memphis, Tenn., Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images This much is for sure: The Lakers need to be aggressive ahead of February’s trade deadline. They have the NBA’s best record at 15-3 They’re the it team. These opportunities don’t come around often. It has been six years since the Lakers won their last championship in 2020. Before that? Ten years had elapsed following their title in 2010. Pelinka is well aware that it’s go time. Sacramento Kings defender Dylan Cardwell plays defense against Los Angeles Lakers player Walker Kessler on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images “We’ll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see,” Pelinka said on Spectrum SportsNet. “We think this team has a real chance to make a run, so we want to give the group as much talent as we can. “Don’t want to get too far over our skis with a hot start, because you don’t want to get big-headed. But clearly the way it’s gone so far, it’s been great. And we hope it continues.” Pelinka spent the offseason building a roster around Doncic, including emptying his treasure chest to acquire Kessler in a sign-and-trade with the Jazz, giving them two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps on top of a four-year, $130 million deal. The Kessler gamble has panned out. He’s a double-double machine. They found their franchise center. But the Lakers are paper thin behind him, with Kevon Looney falling out of the rotation and Jarred Vanderbilt giving bigger teams an advantage. The Lakers must get a backup center. And with their neighbors down the street having a yard sale, Lopez could be a good option for a Lakers team with limited draft capital following the Kessler deal. The Lakers have taken the league by storm this season. They’re the real deal. They have a legitimate shot at winning the Larry O’Brien Championship Trophy. They just have to make sure they plug any holes that could sink them.

stories.title: Yahoo Perfect 5: Victor Wembanyama, Giannis Antetokounmpo lead lineup with piece of every team for Friday's Prime doubleheader
stories.summary: Dan Titus takes you through his lineup construction for Yahoo's Perfect 5 contest for Friday's Prime doubleheader.
stories.detailText: Yahoo Sports is giving fans another way to play fantasy basketball with Perfect 5, a free-to-play game featuring each week's NBA on Prime doubleheader. The rules are simple: pick five players, stay within a $15 budget and rack up fantasy points through scoring, rebounds, assists, defensive stats and 3s. Friday's slate is an NBA Cup Group Play doubleheader: Heat at Knicks (7 p.m. ET) and Lakers at Spurs (9:30 p.m. ET). The injury report is busy again. Karl-Anthony Towns was downgraded to questionable with an abdominal contusion, Andre Drummond is out in concussion protocol and OG Anunoby is out with a calf strain. Giannis Antetokounmpo is probable with groin tendinitis, Austin Reaves is back from a heel bruise and De'Aaron Fox is questionable with a shin injury. Using Yahoo projections, each player's last five games, the betting lines and the latest injury news, I ran 20,000 simulations of the slate against a simulated Yahoo field built from this week's pick rates. I'm pairing the two best fantasy players on the board and spreading the rest of the lineup across all four teams, so I have a stake in every game. Here's my lineup: My Perfect 5 lineup Player Team Salary Projected Points Victor Wembanyama Spurs $5 58.17 Giannis Antetokounmpo Heat $5 53.67 Matisse Thybulle Lakers $2 21.12 Landry Shamet Knicks $2 19.50 Ryan Conwell Heat $1 19.25 Total $15 171.71 This group finished in the top 1% of the simulated field 23.4% of the time and beat every entry in the field in 1.49% of sims, and nobody in the simulated field had these exact five. It holds up whether Towns plays or not: 24.3% of the time in the sims where he played and 21.6% when he sat. Victor Wembanyama – C, San Antonio Spurs – ($5, 61% picked) Wembanyama is the top projection on the board at 58.17 fantasy points. Over his last five games, he's averaged about 68 fantasy points, including 50 points, 18 rebounds, 4 steals and 5 blocks against the Pelicans last Friday, and 44 points with 16 rebounds at Portland on Wednesday. The blocks are what separate him: he's averaging 3.8 a game, and every one is worth three points. You'll want some star exposure in a matchup featuring two of the NBA's best teams. San Antonio is a 6.5-point home favorite, and the 226.5 total is the higher of the two games. Wemby was in the single best lineup in 58% of my sims, more than anyone else. Yes, 61% of the field has him, but fading a player this far ahead of everyone else isn't worth it. Giannis Antetokounmpo – PF, Miami Heat – ($5, 7% picked) This is the pick that makes the lineup. Giannis is projected for 53.67 fantasy points, essentially even with Luka Dončić, but he's on 7% of rosters to Dončić's 58%. He's been a beast in Miami — scoring about 59 fantasy points a game over his last five, including 34 points, 14 rebounds, 8 assists, and 3 blocks against Detroit, and 32 points and 14 rebounds at Philadelphia on Wednesday. He came into this game probable with a groin injury, but that shouldn't be an issue since he played 36 minutes against Philly a couple of days ago. And the Knicks' frontcourt looks weaker than usual: Drummond is out, Anunoby is doubtful and Towns is a game-time call. Matisse Thybulle – SG, Los Angeles Lakers – ($2, 33% picked) Thybulle is the next best defensive-stats play on the slate to Wemby. He's averaging 2.3 steals and a block, and he's turned that into about 26 fantasy points a game over his last five, with at least 2 steals in four of them. He's added some offense too, scoring 14 points in each of his last two games. Reaves's return could trim his minutes a little, but his value comes from defense, not shots, and that holds up even in a smaller role. Landry Shamet – SG, New York Knicks – ($2, 11% picked) Shamet gets this lineup into the early game without paying for a Knicks star whose status is up in the air (Towns). Shamet's averaging about 19 fantasy points over his last five, right on his 19.50 projection. He's played 30-plus minutes in three of his last four games. He should be in more Sixth Man of the Year conversations and, at 11% picked, he's also a cheaper way to get leverage than Klay Thompson, who's on 58% of rosters at the same $2 cost. Ryan Conwell – SG, Miami Heat – ($1, 17% picked) Conwell is the value that makes two $5 stars work. He's projected for 19.25 fantasy points at $1, the best points-per-dollar mark on the slate, and he's played 25-30 minutes in four of his last five games. He doesn't need a big night; 15 to 20 fantasy points from your $1 slot is plenty. He showed up in the optimal lineup in 51% of my sims, more than any player except Wembanyama. The rookie is gaining confidence by the game, so I'll keep riding the wave. Why not Dončić? Dončić is projected for 53.95 fantasy points, but that number was built during a stretch where he's carried the Lakers by himself. Reaves is back Friday after missing five games, and some of the shots and touches Dončić has been soaking up will go back to his running mate. I trimmed his projection about 5% in the sims to account for that. Even at full strength, he'd be a tough sell: he costs the same $5 as Giannis, projects for about the same and is on eight times as many rosters. How close is that to the max? Very close. Using Yahoo's projections, the highest-scoring possible lineup is Wembanyama, Dončić, Thompson, Thybulle and Conwell at 173.75 fantasy points. Mine comes in just 2.04 points behind it. stories.title: Luka Dončić says he asked Lakers front office to acquire Walker Kessler: "I went to them and said, 'I want Walker"'
stories.summary: Kessler, who was acquired by Los Angeles in a sign-and-trade deal with the Jazz this summer, has been key for the Lakers on both ends of the court.
stories.detailText: One of the Los Angeles Lakers' biggest offseason moves is paying off big so far — and Luka Dončić is taking a bit of credit for making it happen. Lakers center Walker Kessler, who was acquired from the Utah Jazz in a sign-and-trade deal in July, has been a key piece of the team on both ends of the court so far this season. And as it turns out, Dončić told ESPN's Dave McMenamin that he played a role in Kessler's arrival in L.A. In McMenamin's profile on Kessler published Friday, Dončić said that he spoke to Rob Pelinka, the Lakers' president of basketball operations and general manager, during the offseason about acquiring the big man from the Jazz. Dončić said that he was inspired by Kessler's impressive defense at the rim after playing against him in previous seasons. "I told them after the season I wanted Walker," Dončić told ESPN, speaking about that offseason conversation. "I think he's a really good player … Obviously, last season he didn't play. He played like five games. Obviously [Utah] kept him out, but just playing against him in the previous years, it was hard to score. He was protecting the rim, he was dominating the paint. So just after the season, I went to them and said, 'I want Walker.'" Dončić credits his burgeoning chemistry with Kessler as a key piece of the team's growth. When speaking about his pick-and-roll with Kessler, Dončić told ESPN: "When we get good at that … we can be really good." In response, Kessler told ESPN that he was honored to have Dončić want him as a teammate. "To have someone like that, with that pedigree, to say, 'Hey, I want that to be our center'... it was incredible," Kessler said. "I was like, 'Wow, this dude, he believes in me. He knows that I can help this team.' It makes you excited to play." In many ways, the Kessler trade was risky: The Lakers sent two unprotected first-round picks (2031 and 2033) and two first-round swaps (2028 and 2030) for the 25-year-old big man, who only played in five games last year after undergoing season-ending shoulder surgery in November 2025. But so far, the move has paid off. Kessler is averaging team-leading 10.8 rebounds and 2.1 blocks per game, and is the Lakers' third-highest scorer with 14 points per game. His 66.9% field-goal percentage is one of the best in the NBA. It's not a huge surprise that Dončić, who is the Lakers' last remaining superstar after the offseason departure of LeBron James, has filled in the role of player-GM. Dončić is the face of the team and the leading scorer, and seems to have gained significant influence in the Lakers front office. After the Kessler trade went through in July, Dončić said at the time that he was "excited" about the addition . Reports at the time indicated that the team was following Dončić's two biggest requests, which were to retain Austin Reaves (who signed a four-year, $185 million extension this summer) and bring in a rim protector like Kessler. The trio of Dončić, Reaves and Kessler have led the Lakers to a 15-3 record to start the season, putting them at the top of the Western Conference.

They have a bottom-five offense, a bottom-five defense, and the second-worst net rating in the NBA behind the Kings. They are one of the worst-shooting teams in the NBA becaue they don’t really have pieces that fit together. Isaiah Joe also had the best game of his brief tenure with the Pistons, leading Detroit with 21 points and looking comfortable knocking down 3-pointers. Detroit can muddle through the season without Cade; they showed it last season, too.
