stories.title: How high can Alperen Sengun climb Rockets historical hierarchy?
stories.summary: Alperen Sengun can be one of the best Rockets of all time
stories.detailText: HOUSTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 26: Alperen Sengun #28 of the Houston Rockets works against Onyeka Okongwu #17 of the Atlanta Hawks during the second half at Toyota Center on October 26, 2026 in Houston, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) | Getty Images Some NBA teams don’t have a distinct best player in franchise history. The Houston Rockets are not one of those teams. I don’t have to say his name. You know who I’m referring to. James Harden is in a class of his own. Joking. I wasn’t born after 2000. It’s Hakeem “The Dream” Olajuwon, and if the answer ever changes, something unspeakably beautiful has happened. Alperen Sengun will not usurp Olajuwon. There’s no sense in even qualifying that statement. It’s ironclad. But how high can he climb in this organization’s historical hierarchy? Sengun can be one of the best Rockets ever Let’s look at the field. First, we’ll disqualify some “also-ran” candidates. Sengun has already surpassed Steve Francis. Next. He’s inevitably going to surpass Yao Ming. Next. Wait…slow down. Accounting for both health and production, Ming’s best season was 2008-09, when he averaged 21.1 points, 10.6 rebounds, and 2.1 blocks per game with a 3.1 Box Plus/Minus (BPM). If not an injury, his 2006-07 season may have been the benchmark, when Ming averaged 25.0 points, 9.4 rebounds, and 2.0 blocks per game, although his 2.4 BPM was pedestrian. As of this writing, Sengun is (almost in) arguably having a better season than Ming ever did. He’s averaging 22.0 points, 9.3 rebounds, and 7.2 assists per game with an 8.7 BPM. A few quick points before this whole article is dedicated to comparing Sengun and Ming. Comparing players across eras is always a questionable process. On a related note, we know that BPM heavily weighs assists from bigs. If Ming played in 2026, he’d likely get more dimes (he was a very good passer, and it would be a way for him to create threes). Also, my brain wants to say Ming was a better defender, but he wasn’t. Ming was a deep drop specialist who’d quite possibly get tarred and feathered in today’s game. Sengun is defending at the level, even switching at times, and doing a lot of stuff Ming couldn’t dream of. I think Sengun has probably passed Ming already, but it’s highly debatable. What’s clearer is that he’s on a trajectory to do so. So who else can he leapfrog? Sengun can join Rockets’ greats Who are the best Rockets in history (after Olajuwon, of course)? For me, Harden has a firm grip on the number two spot, but some would give it to Moses Malone. After those three, it’s Calvin Murphy and Elvin Hayes. There’s a quick, tidy, sledgehammer of an argument to make here. If Sengun is the best player on a Rockets championship team, he automatically gains a strong argument for the number two spot. Yes, “rings culture”. I’m a proponent of the notion that the NBA championship is the existential purpose of the NBA, and that winning a championship, while not the exclusive measure of a player, is the most important one. So, if the Rockets won the title this year: I would consider Sengun the fourth-best Rocket in franchise history. Why fourth? Well, Harden did accomplish some lofty statistical feats. A 10.9 BPM in 2018-19. Thirty-two straight 30-point games, second only to Wilt Chamberlain. A 53-point, 17-assist, and 16-rebound performance (not a typo). And he took the Rockets to Game Seven of the Western Conference Finals against one of the most dynastic teams in NBA history, arguably stifled only by Chris Paul’s hamstring. That’s where ring culture can be myopic: There are variables outside of a player’s control. Similarly, Moses Malone led the team to the NBA Finals and won an MVP. One championship probably doesn’t erase that either. Two would, but let’s all calm down. Elvin Hayes never made it out of the first round during his Rockets tenure. Calvin Murphy did, but he was practically a role player during their 1981 run. I’m not so old as to have seen either (or Malone, just so we’re clear), but statistically, Sengun has surpassed Murphy already. Even a Conference Finals run in 2026-27 could put him ahead of Hayes. If anything, this piece is a testament to the Rockets’ franchise legacy. We (yes, we) can be easy to overlook. We’re not the Lakers, Celtics, Spurs, or Warriors, but we’re in the next tier with the Pistons, Heat, Bucks, and Thunder. We’re a proud middle upperclass team, so the fact that Sengun is even forcing us to consider his place in franchise history is meaningful. If this Rockets core explodes, he can get as high as second. There’s no exact science here, but a pair of titles should get him there. Otherwise, one title, sustained team success, and marginal individual improvement would, in my estimation, get him as high as third. If the Rockets never win a title during his tenure, and he stabilizes at his current level of play, I’d put him fourth or fifth depending on your view of Hayes. Second place is almost surely his ceiling, but there are some bars nobody should expect to clear.

stories.title: Game Preview: The Suns have a Cooper Flagg problem to solve on Black Friday
stories.summary: The Suns and Mavericks are separated by 1.5 games in the standings, giving this matchup significance beyond the NBA Cup.
stories.detailText: PHOENIX, AZ - FEBRUARY 10: Cooper Flagg #32 of the Dallas Mavericks handles the ball during the game against the Phoenix Suns on February 10, 2026 at PHX Arena in Phoenix, Arizona. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Kate Frese/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Who : Phoenix Suns (9-8) vs. Dallas Mavericks (11-7) When : 7:00 pm Arizona Time Where : Mortgage Matchup Center — Phoenix, Arizona Watch : Suns+, 3TV/AZFS Listen : KMVP 98.7 I hope everybody had a memorable and delicious Thanksgiving. Today? We’re back to basketball. The Phoenix Suns, after going 4-1 on their most recent road trip, return home to face the Dallas Mavericks, a team that finds itself at 11-7 and riding a four-game winning streak after starting the season 7-7. It’s a battle between two teams in close proximity in the standings. Dallas currently sits 1.5 games ahead of Phoenix as the eighth seed in the Western Conference, while the Suns, at 9-8, occupy the 10th seed. Games like this carry a little extra weight, and it has little to do with the NBA Cup. For context, the Dallas Mavericks currently lead Group A in the Western Conference with a 3-0 record and a +36 point differential. They’ve already clinched the group and punched their ticket to the knockout rounds. Phoenix, meanwhile, sits at 1-2. So why does this result matter as it pertains to the NBA Cup? If you recall, the reward for advancing in the NBA Cup is an opportunity to win a relatively meaningless trophy while adding games against difficult competition to your schedule. Some willingly embrace that reality, subscribing to the iron sharpens iron methodology and pointing to the fact that the New York Knicks won both the NBA Cup and the NBA championship last season. That’s fair. But some teams, like the Phoenix Suns a season ago, really didn’t have any business being there, and all they ultimately did was add two losses to their schedule. Meanwhile, if you’re a quality team that misses out on advancing in the NBA Cup, there’s a possibility that the two games added to your schedule come against lesser competition, presenting an opportunity to add a pair of wins to your overall record. If the Suns win tonight, they’ll finish group play at 2-2 and could find themselves matched up against another team that finished with a similar record. So there are immediate implications as it pertains to positioning in the Western Conference standings, as well as potential implications for their overall record, knowing that two games could be added to their schedule against competition you might deem beatable. Tale of the Tape Probable Starters Injury Report Suns Mark Williams — OUT (Left Shoulder Surgery) Mavericks Tarik Biberovic — OUT (Right Heel Bursitis) Sergio de Larrea — OUT (Right Knee Sprain) Tobi Lawal — OUT (Right Groin Strain) Dereck Lively II — OUT (Right Foot Surgery) Caleb Martine — AVAILABLE (Right Thumb Splint) What to Watch For Dallas is led by sophomore phenom and former number one overall pick Cooper Flagg, who is averaging 24.3 points per game on 48/32/85 shooting splits, adding 6.7 assists and 6.3 rebounds. He’s young, athletic, and has an affinity for getting to the rim. He ranks ninth in the NBA with 9.5 attempts per game at the rim, so he’s going to force the issue. The Suns need to be ready for it. Cooper Flagg tonight vs Denver: 24 PTS | 6 REB | 12 AST | 8/17 FG | 57 TS% 26.8/5.0/8.3 on 51/46/78 last 4 games 🔥 pic.twitter.com/vyXylY7lZ7 — Basketball Performances (@NBAPerformances) November 25, 2026 Dallas also has Daniel Gafford, who currently leads the league with a 69.5% field goal percentage. My point? Keep an eye on the interior of the Suns’ defense in this one. The Mavericks are a relatively average three-point shooting team, attempting 37.8 threes per game, which ranks 14th in the league, and connecting on 34.4% of them, good for 20th. Phoenix needs to be mindful of both the perimeter and the interior, but more importantly, they need to be smart about how they defend Cooper Flagg. That assignment will most likely fall to either Dillon Brooks or Miles Bridges, and Flagg is clearly more athletic than both of them. I’d almost prefer Bridges on him to introduce another level of physicality, as he has a greater ability to move players off their spots. Brooks’ agility, however, might give him the advantage in that matchup. Ultimately, that’s what I’ll be watching tonight. Who’s guarding Cooper Flagg, and how effective are they in doing so? Key to a Suns Win The Mavericks like to get out and run, and their 18.6 fast break points per game rank second in the NBA. They’re also eighth in the league with 19.4 points off turnovers per game. If you’re careless with the ball against a team that ranks sixth in the league with 9.4 steals per game, they’ll take it and run. The key here? Ball security. No need to give a team like Dallas a chance to cherry-pick points. Dallas also ranks seventh in the league with 16.6 second-chance points per game. I think you know where I’m going with this one. The Suns’ rebounding has been abhorrent through the first 20% of the season. And when you’re playing a team like the Mavericks, who possess plenty of size and can continually bring more of it off the bench, there’s going to be no relenting in that aspect of the game. Box out, rebound, rinse, repeat. We saw that fight against the Houston Rockets, the same fight that defined the Suns’ identity a season ago. The hope is that they bring that same focus and energy tonight and channel some of it into a little give-a-shit on the boards. Prediction This is one of those games that’s going to be a fight, as you have two teams that find themselves in the same neighborhood of the Western Conference standings. And that’s essentially what we have right now: three distinct neighborhoods. You have five teams within 1.5 games of the lead, the sixth through 11th seeds separated by 2.5 games, and then it falls off a cliff. The 12th seed sits five games behind the 11th. After a lengthy road trip, Phoenix is back home in front of a Black Friday crowd that will include me and my family, who are in town from Fresno. The hope is that the crowd isn’t suffering from that post-Thanksgiving malaise and will be loud and proud in support of a team coming off an impressive road trip. I think that’ll be the case. The Suns will feed off that energy, and Jordan Goodwin will hit five three-pointers in this one. Suns win. After the New York Knicks became the first team to win the NBA Cup and Finals in the same season, Jalen Brunson & Co. won't be able to keep their championship run going. NBA commissioner Adam Silver has had a longstanding fascination with European soccer. Establishing an in-season cup competition within the NBA schedule came from soccer leagues having both a regular-season title, won by the team with the most points over the full year, and a separate tournament (or, in some leagues, multiple tournaments) that runs concurrently with the league season. In England, for example, there are the various divisions -- led by the Premier League -- and also the FA Cup competition. But unlike those European leagues, which play their cup competitions outside of their league schedules, the NBA Cup is built in to the regular-season slate. The 30 NBA teams are split into six five-team groups -- three featuring Eastern Conference teams and three comprising Western Conference teams -- with each team then playing one game against the other four in its group. The winner of each group, plus the team with the best record among the non-group winners, advances to the knockout stage of the competition. How will this impact the regular-season schedule and standings? Typically, the NBA sends out a full 82-game schedule in mid-August. Now, the league sends out only 80 games and leaves a gap of roughly a week to fill in later, depending on how the group stage of the NBA Cup plays out. The two teams from the East and West that lose in the quarterfinals will play their 82nd game against each other. Meanwhile, the 22 teams that fail to qualify for the knockout rounds will have their final two games scheduled -- one at home and one on the road against others eliminated in the group stage. The teams that reach the NBA Cup final will actually play 83 games -- though the championship game won't count toward the standings or any statistical markers. The four teams that reach the semifinals will have completed their 82 games and won't need any other games added to their schedule. Any team that makes it to the semifinals will have that game moved later in the schedule to avoid back-to-back games. The NBA made this change in an effort to avoid having empty days on the calendar while attempting to minimize back-to-backs for all teams as much as possible. Where are the semifinals and final being played? In a shift from previous tournaments, the quarterfinals and semifinals will be played at home sites. The Dec. 11 title game, meanwhile, will move from Las Vegas to the storied Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. NBA commissioner Adam Silver previously said the league was searching for "storied college arenas" to play host to the Cup final. (No venue has been announced for 2027.) Why does the NBA Cup include regular-season games? Before its launch, one of the main questions surrounding the in-season tournament was why any team would be incentivized to compete in it. The NBA ensured teams will be motivated by making every game part of the season and, as in-conference matchups, potentially important to playoff tiebreakers. If this had been set up like the cup tournaments in European soccer, there would have been nothing stopping NBA teams from opting out by sitting their top players for extra rest. Which teams make up the groups? To create the groups, the NBA put the 15 teams in each conference into five pots, separated by their finish last season. Pot 1 included the teams that finished in the top three in the regular-season standings, Nos. 4-6 in the standings went into Pot 2, Nos. 7-9 into Pot 3, Nos. 10-12 into Pot 4 and Nos. 13-15 into Pot 5. As a result, the following groups were drawn: East Group A Detroit Pistons Toronto Raptors Orlando Magic Milwaukee Bucks Brooklyn Nets East Group B New York Knicks Cleveland Cavaliers Philadelphia 76ers Miami Heat Indiana Pacers East Group C Boston Celtics Atlanta Hawks Charlotte Hornets Chicago Bulls Washington Wizards West Group A Denver Nuggets Houston Rockets Phoenix Suns Dallas Mavericks Utah Jazz West Group B Oklahoma City Thunder Minnesota Timberwolves LA Clippers New Orleans Pelicans Memphis Grizzlies West Group C San Antonio Spurs Los Angeles Lakers Portland Trail Blazers Golden State Warriors Sacramento Kings Does one group stand out the most from the others? East Group B is a monster. All five teams -- defending NBA Cup and Finals champion New York, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Miami and Indiana -- are among the favorites to win the conference in 2026-27. The group stage will also feature reunion games for LeBron James , when the 76ers face the Cavs and Heat. And after guard Tyrese Haliburton missed the entire 2025-26 season while rehabbing a torn Achilles, the Pacers will be back among the East elite and hungry to reach the title game in Indianapolis. What do players get for winning? In 2023, the first year the tournament was held, the players on the winning team received $500,000 each and the runners-up got $200,000. The losing players of the semifinals each got $100,000, and those ousted in the quarterfinals got $50,000. Now, in each subsequent year, the prizes will be slightly higher, as a result of negotiated raises year over year to keep pace with increases in the salary cap and basketball-related income as part of the most recent collective bargaining agreement between the NBA and the National Basketball Players Association. Will anyone earn individual honors for their play in NBA Cup games? There will be an MVP award, as well as an all-tournament team. Will this have any impact on the playoffs? Not beyond the games counting in the regular-season standings (and toward tiebreakers). The only playoff impact comes from the wins and losses accrued throughout the tournament. Though there was debate among league insiders about guaranteeing a playoff berth for winning the tournament, ultimately that idea (or any other to further incentivize teams) was not enacted. Why is it called the Emirates NBA Cup? The league struck a sponsorship deal with Emirates, the Dubai-based airline, to sponsor the tournament after its initial run. The NBA said last year that it went with the most basic titles for both the tournament and its trophy -- the "in-season tournament" and "NBA Cup" -- as a way to introduce the concept to fans. However, using such nondescript names had another clear advantage: It gave the league a blank slate in case it sold the naming rights for the tournament and cup to a sponsor and avoided the complications that could arise by naming them after someone (for example, late NBA commissioner David Stern, one possibility that had been floated before the tournament was officially unveiled). (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to the Game Thread. Veterans of the Game Thread know how we do things around here, but for all you newbies we have a few rules. Our community guidelines apply and basically say be cool, no personal attacks, don’t troll and don’t swear too much. The Spurs lost their first road game and NBA Cup game of the season on Wednesday night, in a 111-106 thriller in front of an enthusiastic Moda Center crowd as both Dame and Deni Avdija went nuclear and out-executed the Silver and Black down the final stretch. Some missed free throws, a lane violation and an 8 second violation were costly as the Spurs ran the gamut of rarely enforced reasons to lose points at a key juncture of the game. The Spurs missed having De’Aaron Fox available, as his quickness and steady administration of the offensive sets was missed, especially in crunch time. Dylan Harper’s absence was apparent, too, with the Spurs were missing his ability to get points even when the offense was not creating any space. The Spurs became too reliant on three point shooting, which isn’t good for them, because only Champagnie is a good three-point shooter among the rotation players, and everybody in the Moda Center knew that, especially the Trail Blazer defenders. The good news is that Fox should be back in tonight’s lineup. The better news is that Harper is listed as questionable on the injury report, which means that he could return to play tonight, just 10 days since fell on the court and injured his hip with less than a minute left in the Pistons game. Harper’s injury was initially estimated to keep him out from 1-3 weeks (or 2-3 weeks, depending on where you read the news) and he’s definitely on the lower end of that estimate. Tonight, they face the Los Angeles Lakers in their final game of the Emirates Cup group stage. The math is pretty simple. In order to advance to the knockout rounds, they will have to beat the Lakers tonight. Because the Trail Blazers won on Wednesday, they will win the group and automatically advance if they win tonight’s game against the Warriors, which tips off at the same time as the Lakers/Spurs game. In that case, a win for the Silver and Black would send them to the quarterfinals as the group winners, with a home game on December 4 or 5. If the Blazers win tonight, then the Spurs would probably advance to the semis as the Western Conference wild card, because they would have the best point differential among the second place finishers, barring some unlikely scenarios like the Grizzlies defeating the Timberwolves by 40+ or the Nuggets routing the Jazz by 50+ [OK, the second one could happen]. If the Spurs are the wild card, they will play on the road against the top team in the west, which would probably be the Wolves or Mavericks. Is that all clear? Probably not. But if the Spurs lose tonight, it’s even simpler. They will join the also-rans and have two more games added to the schedule in the second week of December against other non-qualifying teams. Although it’s probably marginally better for the Spurs overall record, having two games against mediocre opponents added to the schedule than having to play two teams against top four teams in the conference, it would be a disappointment to a team that’s looking to prove that they’re ready to compete for the NBA title again this season. Last year, the top two teams in the NBA Cup were the teams in the NBA Finals, and that could happen again this season. A lot of times, you can refer to the best player on the opponents’ team as “the head of the snake.” That’s not exactly true of Luka Doncic. He’s not the head of the snake, he’s the whole damn snake. His usage rate is insanely high, and the rest of the team is pretty much relegated to watching him work on the offensive end. If the Spurs can force him to give up the ball early, and make the Lakers run the offense through someone else, especially if it’s not Austin Reaves [questionable with a bruised heel], then the Spurs can hold down their scoring. The Lakers defense is decent, but the Spurs offense will be fine if they move the ball and don’t just settle for three point shots. Let’s GO SPURS!! Castle must dominate Luka. Victor Wembanyama, who was standing 6 feet away during the incident, will be called for a blocking foul. teamStories.detailText: Austin Reaves will return to the Los Angeles Lakers' lineup for their NBA Cup matchup with the San Antonio Spurs on Friday. He is listed as available on the team's injury report. Reaves, 28, has been sidelined since suffering a bruised heel in a Nov. 11 win over the Milwaukee Bucks. At the time, the Lakers believed Reaves' injury wasn't serious and didn't require imaging. Head coach JJ Redick said the guard was day-to-day. However, he missed the team's next five games. During that five-game span, the Lakers went 4-1 while facing lesser teams including the Charlotte Hornets (4-13), Utah Jazz (3-16) and Sacramento Kings (2-16). In 12 games this season, Reaves is averaging 24.7 points per game, second behind Luka Dončić, who leads the league with an average of 36.6 points. He's also averaging 4.7 assists and 1.2 steals while shooting 41% on 66 3-point attempts. The Spurs also could get guards De'Aaron Fox and Dylan Harper back for Friday's game. Both are listed as questionable. The Lakers go into Friday's matchup with the NBA's best record at 15-3 , a half-game ahead of the 15-4 Spurs. In the NBA Cup standings , both teams have a 2-1 record in the Western Conference's Group C. San Antonio would win the group with a win and the Portland Trail Blazers losing to the Golden State Warriors. However, with a +48 point differential, the Spurs could still advance on a tiebreaker. The Lakers would prevail with a victory and a Warriors loss. But a defeat would eliminate them from the in-season tournament.

The shooting guard was playing for the Lakers during the start of a nine-game winning streak that was snapped by the Utah Jazz on Nov. 18. He's missed the last five games for Los Angeles, but the Lakers went 4-1 without him in the lineup during that stretch. Reaves provides some relief despite the success, adding another proven scorer to the lineup. It could also allow for the team to be less reliant on Luka Doncic, who has averaged 36.2 minutes per game, the second-highest average in his career. stories.title: Bo Nix, after one of his worst games for Broncos, says 'I let the team down'
stories.summary: After one of the most difficult starts of his NFL career, Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said "I let the team down'' in a 27-5 loss to the Steelers on Friday.
stories.detailText: PITTSBURGH -- After one of the most difficult starts of his NFL career, Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said "I let the team down'' in a 27-5 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday. The Broncos' first Black Friday game certainly won't go in Nix's scrapbook -- or the offense's -- as the Broncos mustered just 205 net yards, with a Nix fumble recovered for a touchdown and one of his two interceptions returned for a touchdown. "It's frustrating for sure and I let the team down,'' Nix said. "[That is] the last thing I want to do as a quarterback, as a leader of the team ... [My teammates] didn't let me get too down. I was wanting to get a little more down than they were letting me.'' In a game played in a steady rain with a windchill of 29 degrees at kickoff, Nix finished 22-of-49 passing for 169 yards and was sacked three times, with the three turnovers. It was the first time in Nix's 47 career starts (including regular season and playoffs) he had three turnovers and was sacked three times in the same game. The struggles in the rain were reminiscent of a 10-9 win over the Jets in 2024, his rookie year; Nix finished with a career-low 60 yards passing at a rain-swept MetLife Stadium. The Broncos' 204 net yards Friday were their third fewest this season, behind 176 net yards in the season-opening loss at Kansas City and 168 in a Week 6 win over Seattle . Broncos coach Sean Payton was quick to provide cover for Nix, pointing the finger more at his playcalls that led to the first-half turnovers. "Starts with me,'' Payton said. "Early on we gave them opportunities with momentum and that falls on me.'' Nix and Payton circled the QB's first-quarter fumble as one of those opportunities for the Steelers. Especially in a week when the Steelers were in the national swirl of the benching -- and eventual waiving -- of quarterback Aaron Rodgers, as well as Rodgers' takedown of Steelers coach Mike McCarthy in an interview on "The Pat McAfee Show." But in a scoreless game, with the Broncos' offense already sputtering, Denver faced a third-and-15 from its own 19-yard line. After the snap, the Broncos tried to set up a screen pass to running back Tyler Badie , but the Steelers had multiple defenders quickly beat blocks, and defensive tackle Keeanu Benton quickly dropped to get in the passing lane in front of Badie. As Nix tried to reset after he saw Badie covered, he lost the ball, and T.J. Watt recovered it in the end zone. The touchdown brought the Steelers crowd into full-throated support that never dissipated. "Going down 7-0, with a fumble recovered for a touchdown is definitely not ideal,'' Nix said. "That started us off on the wrong foot and we could never get out of the hole. ... Momentum is a real thing.'' "I'm kicking myself for the first score,'' Payton said. "You know, we're running a screen play, but it's a slower developing screen play, and coming out [from near the end zone], that's not too good. ... This is one of those games, 10 points [Friday] is different than 10 points on any normal -- 10 points is a lot -- so a seven-point swing, they score on defense, that's why I kick myself relative to a few of those calls.'' It didn't get much better for Nix or the offense the rest of the way. With 1:44 left in the first half, on a first-and-10 from the Broncos' own 28-yard line, Nix tried to fit a ball to Jaylen Waddle up the right sideline. But Nix was short on the throw, and Jalen Ramsey returned the interception 36 yards for a touchdown that gave the Steelers a 24-5 lead. "I saw [Ramsey], I just didn't throw it high enough over his head,'' Nix said. "Once they got 14-0 momentum, it's tough, that's not what you want to do on the road against a good team. A good team is not going to let you back in.'' Nix thew his second interception in the fourth quarter, with just under nine minutes left. The loss means the Broncos (8-3) lost a chance to nudge a game in front of the Kansas City Chiefs (8-3) in the AFC West and puts them two games behind the Buffalo Bills (10-1) in the quest for home-field advantage. The Broncos face the Bills on Christmas in Denver.

stories.title: Aaron Rodgers calls out Tom Brady for comments on locker room ‘sanctity’
stories.summary: Rodgers drew the criticism of Brady — and numerous analysts around the NFL — after his appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show” on Wednesday.
stories.detailText: Aaron Rodgers called out Tom Brady after his messy Steelers divorce. Aaron Rodgers appeared to call out Tom Brady’s “sanctity of an NFL locker room” comment in a text to Al Michaels that the Prime Video play-by-play broadcaster read during the Steelers’ win over the Broncos on Friday. “A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room, [Rodgers] said, ‘The code of sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership,’” Michaels said, reading the message from Rodgers, which also included a claim that he was “barred” from the Pittsburgh facility. Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) looks to pass against the Indianapolis Colts in Pittsburgh, Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. Getty Images Rodgers drew the criticism of Brady — and numerous analysts around the NFL — after his appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show” on Wednesday, during which he accused Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings, breaking down a halftime huddle with “1-2-3 Packers” and missing walkthroughs. The comments followed the Steelers’ decision to start Rudolph and make Rodgers inactive, which they announced Tuesday night. And while Rodgers never referenced Brady by name in his message to Michaels, the “sanctity” line was the exact phrase that the former Patriots and Buccaneers star used. Former NFL player Tom Brady looks on prior to a game between the Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers in Minneapolis, Sunday, Dec. 29, 2024. Getty Images “The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it’s a very sacred place,” Brady said Thursday on the Fox broadcast. “We shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players. It’s a privilege to be in that locker room. You’re fighting with your teammates, you’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together. Shouldn’t always be the place for private things to become public, that’s what I’ll say.” Brady overlapped with Rodgers in the NFL for most of his career before shifting into broadcasting after retirement, and it’s unclear if Rodgers might need to contemplate a similar move after he was released by the Steelers on Wednesday. The 42-year-old cleared waivers , but according to Prime Video reporter and NFL insider James Palmer on Thursday, teams have expressed little to no interest in signing Rodgers for the remainder of the season. And for one night, the Steelers thrived without Rodgers , as a pair of defensive touchdowns and one touchdown pass from Rudolph improved their record to 7-4.

stories.summary: Brock Purdy did not practice all week with a mid ankle sprain he suffered against the Vikings. Kyle Shanahan is optimistic his QB will be back soon.
stories.detailText: The San Francisco 49ers will be without their quarterback for the first of their two-game NFC West leg this week. Brock Purdy has been ruled out for their Week 12 divisional matchup against the Seattle Seahawks , head coach Kyle Shanahan announced on Friday, Nov. 27. Mac Jones will get the start at home against the defending Super Bowl champions. Purdy sprained his left ankle in the second quarter of the Mexico City game against the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 22, though he kept playing and finished with 255 passing yards and three touchdowns in a 35-10 win to push the Niners' NFL-best record to 9-1. He did not practice all week while nursing his ankle and despite Shanahan's optimism that he wouldn't miss time, Purdy is now being shut down for the week after it was revealed he suffered a mid-ankle sprain, which typically is slower to heal. Shanahan told reporters Friday that Purdy won't require surgery. Does he expect his franchise QB back next week against the Los Angeles Rams ? "It's too soon, but I mean I'm pretty optimistic about it," he said. "But I was (optimistic) about this week to start and then it changes, so hopefully it'll be all right." Without Purdy, the Niners have been in good hands with Jones, who went 5-3 in eight games started a year ago when Purdy went down with a toe injury. In those eight games, Jones threw 13 touchdowns for 2,151 yards with six interceptions and a 97.4 passer rating. The Seahawks , on the other hand, are no stranger to quarterback injuries this year. They'll have Sam Darnold back on Sunday from a quad injury that kept him out of their last two games. Though the 49ers are tied with the Chicago Bears for most wins in the league with nine, these next two divisional games against the third-place Seahawks and second-place Rams will be crucial as they lead LA by 2 1/2 games in the ultracompetitive NFC West. stories.title: Steelers players express support for Mike McCarthy after winning first game since Aaron Rodgers divorce
stories.summary: The Steelers had some things to discuss after Aaron Rodgers unleashed a laundry list of grievances against the head coach.
stories.detailText: It can't be denied the Pittsburgh Steelers are a different team after one of the most eventful weeks of the season, but that apparently isn't all bad. A number of Steelers players expressed their support for head coach Mike McCarthy in the aftermath of a 27-5 win over the Denver Broncos on Black Friday , the team's first game since a very public divorce with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers. The saga saw Rodgers make several claims while appearing on "The Pat McAfee Show" that painted McCarthy as disconnected at best and dangerously incompetent at worst after the Steelers benched him, and shortly before they released him. It's a situation with a little precedent in the NFL, and it led to all eyes on McCarthy and the Steelers in Week 12. That is a happy head coach 🤩 #BlackFridayNFL pic.twitter.com/oiFmzOqN8D — NFL on Prime Video (@NFLonPrime) November 27, 2026 Behind the scenes, there was plenty of talking. James Palmer of NFL Network reported before the game that the team's leadership council — a group of veteran players who regularly meet with McCarthy — met on Wednesday and held an "airing of grievances" to address some of the stuff Rodgers was talking about. The meeting reportedly left McCarthy "humbled," but also allowed him to explain to the players why he handled everything the way he did. The meeting apparently left the team on firmer footing, with Steelers cornerback Jalen Ramsey saying the team expressed its support to McCarthy : "For the past couple days, we as players, we were like, 'Coach, you good.' Let us turn this up, let us get in our zone." Quarterback Mason Rudolph, Rodgers' replacement under center, also said the players were behind McCarthy : "I think the leadership council rallied around coach McCarthy. I think in a weird way, the adversity probably brought us closer together. We've just got to keep carrying that in week to week." McCarthy, meanwhile, seemed happy with how the team responded : "Everything that was discussed was healthy. Lot of things in there, but what came out of it was urgency. I thought our leaders did a tremendous job of bringing the urgency to their rooms and it definitely showed up." Mike McCarthy admits Aaron Rodgers was right about one thing One particular point of criticism from Rodgers was that McCarthy had allegedly spent little time engaging with the Pittsburgh defense, despite the quarterback advising that he should. McCarthy's background is almost purely on the offense and he's well known to prioritize that side of the ball while leaving the rest to his defensive coordinator. McCarthy actually admitted Rodgers was right about his lack of focus on the defense: "I have not spent enough time with the defense. That's something as far as job responsibility, job description, these are things that will be looked at in the offseason, but it's a point where in our year, we're making adjustments. Definitely conscientious of it." Steelers defensive end T.J. Watt indicated the players spoke to McCarthy about that, and the results were encouraging : "Mike just admitted that he has got to spend some more time with the defense. We've had a lot of really good conversations, especially recently, and look forward to continuing to build off of what you saw tonight." Mike McCarthy had a tough week, but got a win. AP Photo/Gene J. Puskar Steelers veterans praise Mason Rudolph for stepping up The Steelers veterans also had plenty of praise for Rudolph, whose experience with the team goes back to 2018. Watt didn't seem surprised he was ready for the game: "Mason Rudolph is a true professional. He's been a true professional since I've known him. A guy that's trained like the starter no matter how long he's been here, whether he's the backup or the starter. We have extreme belief in him and he's a great locker room glue guy." Rudolph didn't exactly light up the scoreboard against Denver, but he was at least efficient, going 9-for-15 for 142 yards, 1 touchdown and 0 interceptions. It was a run-heavy game script with the Steelers leading 14-0 after the first quarter and by multiple scores for the rest of the game. Still, Steelers defensive tackle Cameron Heyward noticed Rudolph doing what was needed: "He's ready for all those moments. He understand that with everything that went on, he couldn't have a drop-off. I'm just appreciative to have a guy who when s*** hits the fan, he's able to say, 'Alright, I've gotta step up.'" It was a strong performance at least compared to, well, the standard Rodgers set during the season. NFL Network's Michael Florio noted his 0.19 EPA per dropback, an advanced stat measuring offensive efficiency, was the second-best mark by a Steelers quarterback all season. Rodgers exceeded that level only once all season, in Week 3 against the Cincinnati Bengals. Mike McCarthy thankful for support McCarthy did at one point go out of his way to note "I'm the offensive play-caller," a notable statement given that Rodgers reportedly gave the Steelers an ultimatum that the team give him offensive play-calling duties or release him. However, he seemed far more interested in moving on with the team as constructed, and said he was grateful for the response to a turbulent week: "There's a lot going on. Anytime you're in a situation where time is taken away from winning and your team responds, it is extremely important and gratifying. The reality of this game — and it will always be as far as my approach — this is a players' game. We have a very important role in this sport, but you have to make sure you keep it about the players. We still have work to do from my position and we'll continue to do that. We've just got to keep building off things that we've done well. "We got the win today. It was definitely a hard travel week for us as a football team. I'm proud of our players. I'm proud of our coaching staff. I'm proud of our support staff and I really appreciate all the other support." All of that isn't to say McCarthy's players weren't directly repudiating Rodgers, who passed along his own thoughts via Al Michaels during the game . Star wide receiver DK Metcalf even signaled support to the quarterback via sign language during the first quarter .

stories.title: 49ers rule QB Brock Purdy (ankle) out; Mac Jones to start vs. Seahawks
stories.summary: 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy (ankle) will not play Sunday against the Seahawks, according to coach Kyle Shanahan, paving the way for Mac Jones to start.
stories.detailText: SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy (ankle) will not play Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks , according to coach Kyle Shanahan. After the Niners wrapped up their third and final session of the week, Shanahan said Purdy has officially been ruled out against the Seahawks. Mac Jones will start in Purdy's place with Kurtis Rourke as his backup. "Anytime it's not a high ankle sprain, you get pretty relieved, but it was more mid than low, which is a little bit worse," Shanahan said Friday. "Kind of had a feeling just the way it was by the time Wednesday came around. [It] didn't heal up as fast as we wanted, so had to shut him down." Purdy initially injured his left ankle in the second quarter of last week's win against the Minnesota Vikings . The injury appeared to happen with about 30 seconds left in the opening half when Purdy tried to escape Vikings defensive lineman Jalen Redmond . As a flag for intentional grounding came out, Purdy's left ankle appeared to bend under Redmond as he took him to the ground. Shanahan said Wednesday he knew about Purdy's injury at halftime, and it did not affect his playcalling over the final two quarters. After initially expressing optimism that Purdy would be OK to play against the Seahawks, Shanahan said the injury simply didn't improve enough during the week. Shanahan said surgery is not necessary for Purdy and the hope is he can return for Week 13 against the New York Giants . "It's too soon [to tell] but I'm pretty optimistic about it," Shanahan said. "But I was about this week to start and then it changes. So, hopefully it'll be all right." Jones started eight games in Purdy's stead in 2025 when Purdy dealt with a turf toe injury. The 49ers went 5-3 in those contests with Jones posting a 62.7 QBR with 2,151 passing yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions. Unlike last year, Jones has appeared only in mop-up duty behind Purdy this season with one completion on as many attempts for 5 yards. When Jones jumped into the lineup last year, it happened in Week 2 against the New Orleans Saints . At the time, Jones said getting in early was helpful, but he also has experience taking over the starting role later in the season. He said he hopes to draw on that experience against Seattle. "It's obviously a challenge when you're getting thrown in towards the end of the year, but it's a challenge that I've done before in my career," Jones said. "I'm definitely up for the challenge and looking forward to it." Left tackle Trent Williams said Friday the Niners have plenty of confidence in Jones after his performance in Purdy's place in 2025. "He was great last year when we needed him," Williams said. "We expect him to be good this year." Other teams showed interest in Jones as a trade candidate in the offseason and again leading into November's trade deadline. But the Niners held firm on wanting significant compensation for him and ultimately did not trade him. The Niners took that approach in order to have trustworthy insurance for Purdy, who has missed games with injury in each of the past two seasons. Shanahan said the team never received any concrete offers close enough to justify moving on from Jones, who is in the final year of his 49ers contract. "Anytime you have a backup quarterback who you believe could be one of the better starters in this league, that's a hell of a deal," Shanahan said. "It's always hard and tempting if someone offers a lot of stuff because you know how much that can help your team, but you're kind of glad you don't have to make that decision because of how bad it is when the starter gets hurt and you're missing that guy. Really grateful that he's here and I'm glad we didn't make a trade." For his part, Jones said he viewed the trade deadline as though the 49ers just traded for him and now he's starting a few weeks after it, much like what would have happened had he actually been dealt. "That's how I looked at it," Jones said. "I've been here for a few weeks and now I'm getting my first start. ... Every time I've talked about it or wanted something, it's happened and that's just the way God works, and you've got to be ready for your opportunity." Elsewhere on the injury report, the Niners also ruled out receiver Jordan Watkins , who suffered a groin injury against the Vikings. Wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles), linebacker Dre Greenlaw (neck), safety Siran Neal (knee/foot), cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder/neck) and offensive tackle Austen Pleasants (knee) are questionable.

stories.title: Sam Darnold 'ready to roll' vs. 49ers as Seahawks fight to stay in NFC West race
stories.summary: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold, who missed the past two games with a quad injury, will return to start against the Niners in a pivotal NFC West showdown.
stories.detailText: RENTON, Wash. -- After playing through a cracked rib and then missing the past two games because of a quad injury, quarterback Sam Darnold is back in the Seattle Seahawks ' starting lineup in time for their most pivotal matchup of the season. Coach Mike Macdonald confirmed Friday that Darnold will start Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium, a game the Seahawks must win to keep any realistic hope alive of staying in the NFC West race. "I feel really good," Darnold said Friday after practicing as a full participant for the third straight day. "I'm not going to compare it to any other point in the season, but I feel really good right now." The Seahawks ruled out right tackle Abraham Lucas (ankle), left guard Quenton Nelson (knee) and defensive tackle Jarran Reed (toe). In addition to Darnold, they'll get left tackle Charles Cross (ankle) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger) back. Macdonald had said earlier in the week that the plan was for Darnold to start against the 49ers (9-1) as long as all went well Wednesday in a full-speed practice that followed a lighter session the Seahawks (6-4) had Monday as they returned from their bye. "Sam did a great job," Macdonald said. "We got through Wednesday, so we're ready to roll." Said offensive coordinator Brian Fleury: "He looked great, honestly. It's hard to believe he missed a few weeks and was not throwing and stuff like that. They did a great job with him during the bye week, making sure he was going to be ready to go, and so he looks fantastic." Darnold missed the Seahawks' wins over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9 and Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10 because of a quad injury he suffered near the end of Seattle's loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 8. Darnold also suffered a cracked rib against the Bears on his first dropback of the night. Darnold said "everyday-life things," such as lying in bed, were difficult for several days because of his cracked rib, but that he could throw shortly after suffering the injury. He said he could have continued to play through it, as he did against Chicago, if not for the quad injury. "There's times throughout the season where you're going to have to play through a little bit of pain, but I've dealt with stuff like that throughout every season," he said. "I'm sure everyone does. So, that's just something you've got to deal with sometimes, and I felt like it was manageable to be able to go out there and still perform to a level to where I felt like it was important to be out there." Darnold said he'll have a bit of extra rib padding Sunday but that it won't be too different from what he normally wears. Darnold hurt his quad while escaping the pocket to avoid a blitzing linebacker on Seattle's second-to-last play against the Bears. He said he had to replicate that kind of movement to know that he was ready to return. "Whether it's running to the right or running to the left, making a quick decision to run and throw, kind of that quick-twitch, explosive movement that I need to have when I'm on the move and decide all of the sudden that I need to pull the trigger," he said, "because that takes a lot of torque coming from the ground up." After guiding the Seahawks to a win in Super Bowl LX last February, Darnold has had a tumultuous 2026 season. He also missed most of the first two games because of a glute injury that he suffered on the fifth play of the opener. In six full games, he has thrown nine interceptions and 10 touchdown passes. His Total QBR of 50.1 ranked 23rd from Week 3 to Week 8, and Seattle went 2-4 in that span. Seattle won all four games this season in which Drew Lock stepped in for Darnold. "I feel like I haven't really thought [much about] the year that it's been," Darnold said. "I'm really just focusing on trying to get my body healthy and ready to go, and this week now, putting a game plan together and going and getting ready to play. I'm just really focused on that. I haven't had much time to kind of sit back and think about whether it's been tough or whatnot throughout the early part of the season." The Seahawks are three games back of the NFC West-leading 49ers, who beat them at Lumen Field in Week 5. Two of Darnold's nine interceptions came in that 32-29 loss to San Francisco. He was also sacked five times in that game. Darnold's goal in the rematch, he said, is to play decisively and protect the ball. "When they want to pressure, they do a good job of pressuring and matching the coverage with it, but when they don't pressure, their front does a really good job of getting to the quarterback and making them feel like the pocket is squeezing a little bit," Darnold said of San Francisco's defense. "So, they do a great job, and they did it in our game. But again, for me, it's just about getting the ball out of my hands and understanding when I do have time to be able to hold it and take my shot, but also understanding that the ball's got to get out."

stories.title: Steelers credit T.J. Watt, Cam Heyward for leadership amidst adverse week
stories.summary: T.J. Watt, Cam Heyward, and Jalen Ramsey helped lead the Steelers out of a dark week
stories.detailText: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers responded to a very adverse week by dominating the Denver Broncos 27-5 to get to 7-4 and remain unbeaten at home in 2026. It was a trying week for the Steelers, who released quarterback Aaron Rodgers after he demanded to take over play-calling duties. Rodgers then went on The Pat McAfee Show and put head coach Mike McCarthy on blast for falling asleepp in meetings, missing walk throughs, and not getting to know defensive players, among other things. In trying times like this, teams lean on their leaders, and several players credited T.J. Watt and Cam Heyward for the work they did with the team this week. “I thought TJ and Cam did a really good job before the game,” Pat Freiermuth said via Brooke Pryor . “Really talking about it’s bigger than one person, it’s bigger than two people… It’s about the Rooney family and the Steelers and the fans, and they deserve our best effort today.” Safety Jaquan Brisker echoed those sentiments. “We had a very important leadership council meeting this week, and we all were in there and talked about keeping this team together and turning the page,” Brisker said via Nick Farabaugh . Quarterback Mason Rudolph, who threw a touchdown pass in the win, pointed out how lucky the Steelers are to have superstars with high leadership abilities. “Your average team doesn’t have a Cam Heyward or a T.J. Watt or a Jalen Ramsey,” Rudolph said . “Those guys did an awesome job at just pointing the trajectory of where the team needed to go. Pittsburgh took a bunch of cannonball shots this week, but it’s clear their foundation is strong due to the leaders they have inside their locker room. They will now get ready for a Week 13 matchup with the Houston Texans next week on Sunday Night Football. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! stories.title: Undrafted rookie could be the Rams best option at tight end
stories.summary: Dan Villari has playmaker potential, is he ready?
stories.detailText: After making a move towards multiple tight ends late last season, it was not surprising that the Los Angeles Rams brought eight tight ends into OTAs and kept them all through training camp. L.A. finally decided to keep five, a higher than average number, on the opening roster. They also kept around another tight end, prospect Dan Villari, on the practice squad. Spring forward to the end of November and the Rams deep tight end room has been thinned substantially by injuries. Terrance Ferguson is out for the year; Colby Parkinson has missed one full game, parts of another half-dozen, and obviously impaired in many others; Davis Allen has a high ankle sprain, which carries a normal recovery time of a minimum of four weeks; and now Tyler Higbee has been designated as week-to-week with a bruised chest. Against the Green Packers on Thanksgiving Eve, the Rams installed offensive tackle David Quessenberry as tight end in the “13” personnel groupings. With the cupboard near bare, is Dan Villari the next best option? Villari, 24 years-old, was signed by the Rams as a 2026 undrafted free agent out of Syracuse, but his journey to the NFL did not begin as a tight end. Originally recruited and signed as a quarterback by Michigan, he spent two seasons with the Wolverines. After a redshirt, he appeared in four 2021 games, recording one completion in three attempt and running for 35 yards on nine carries. TE Dan Villari continues to make his case for the NFL. At Pro Day today, his time of 7.04 seconds in the three-cone drill was faster than any tight end at the NFL Combine, per SU Athletics. His 20-yard shuttle time of 4.31 seconds would have been second-best at the Combine pic.twitter.com/gfRPjWlTsj — Ashley Wenskoski (@AshleyWenskTV) March 16, 2026 Transferred to Syracuse for 2022 and the Orangemen converted him to tight end in summer workouts. Over four seasons, he played in 44 games with 25 starts, catching 64 passes for 671 yards. In 2023 and 24, Syracuse, lined him up all over the field, collecting reps at running back and quarterback to go along with tight end duties. For his career, he chipped in 484 rushing yards at a 4.9 per carry clip and completed 23 of 33 passes for 177 yards. It’s fair to label him as a receiver first prospect. At 6’4” 243 lb.Villari is not a towering tight end like the rest of the unit. He sports just-above average arm length at 32 1/4” and owns good-sized hands, 9 3/4”. On film, Villari looks like a fluid athlete. At his Pro Day, he didn’t test in any of the explosive/strength drills, vertical, broad jump, or bench press. Bit of a discrepancy in the reporting of his forty yard dash times, RAS reports 4.77 with a 1.66 10-yard split, while others put him at a hand-timed 4.60. A 7.04 3cone shows stellar agility and flexibility. Burst and balance were excellent as well, 4.31 shuttle. College film shows, even with his lack of experience, the looks of a natural fit at tight end. Primarily lined up in the slot, he gets to his spot and gives his quarterback a nice square target. Nice feel for open space. I have to describe his hands as iron in velvet, soft because the football just seems to be absorbed into his grip and strong because he plucks passes with his hands away from his body and tucks them away quickly. Solid wingspan and body control to haul in awry balls. Fearless over the middle and catches well through contact. As an open-field runner, I’d use “competitive” as the descriptor, he gets north/south in a hurry and runs low behind his pads, often right through first contact, Blocking needs a lot of technique and strength work. He’s willing, but doesn’t have much pop in his strikes and lacks the needed handwork/arm extension. Came into the pros as a developmental prospect, but you can see he has the base traits. Villari has been on the receiving end of passes just three short years. He offers interesting versatility, although it would be highly suspect if the Rams would build a package of plays around an undrafted player joining the team this late in proceedings. He did however, run the ball out of wildcat formation, throws pretty well, and has very good hands. Like almost all youngsters, he needs route-running polish, but Villari’s short area agility and natural move skills hint that he can handle a bigger route tree. Most of his targets were of the simpler variety, pivots, look-in/curls, and up the seams. In actuality, the current L.A. tight ends don’t appear to be running a particularly complicated route tree either. Syracuse TE Dan Villari has some of the most impressive route running chops & stem work in this class. SMU game was one of his best. When QB Steve Angeli went down, Villari fell under the radar, but he's got high-level foot speed, decel, & hip sink. Senior Bowl riser candidate. pic.twitter.com/6iPNtxkeoJ — Ian Cummings (@IC_Draft) January 20, 2026 Roster fill or value add? The Rams preseason lack of urgency in adding wide receiver depth hinted they’re were going to make use of tight ends in the slot akin to receivers as a regular part of the rotation. Things have since changed due to all the injuries. Of the remaining two fully-available tight ends remaining, Parkinson can, and has been split out, but he’s a bit heavy-footed and best suited closer to the action, while Max Klare is more natural to the slot, in skills, size, and athletically. Villari game appears more apt to fit in with Klare’s. Circumstances have certainly conspired against the Rams ball catchers, both wide outs and tight ends. Sean McVay would really be up against it if he were to try shapeshifting the offense again, back into three wide receiver sets. There doesn’t appear to be many answers there. The L.A. braintrust looks limited in their options. At tight end, they will likely need to add a body. It could be a street retread or giving Villari a shot. Update: The Rams are reportedly poaching TE Jack Stoll off the 49ers practice squad At $45k guaranteed, Villari was the Rams highest paid undrafted rookie in 2026, there must be more than “roster filler” interest, Yes indeed, he joined the team needing development and strength/conditioning work, but he’s now been in the program for seven months, working on strength, technique and getting a grasp off the playbook. There is likely little or no upgrade available at this point. In theory, McVay and tight ends coach Scott Huff could kick the tires on Villari, he has three practice squad elevations to the active roster, before a permanent decision needs to be made on his future. Elevated or signed, the Rams need to activate Dan Villari.

stories.title: Steelers locker room 'prideful' but muted after win amid Aaron Rodgers firestorm
stories.summary: The tight end rallied the team with a fiery speech after one of his best friends was released for criticizing coach Mike McCarthy.
stories.detailText: PITTSBURGH – Pat Freiermuth found himself in the center of the mess involving the Steelers and now-former quarterback Aaron Rodgers this week. Rodgers told ESPN’s “Pat McAfee Show” that the veteran tight end was the player who informed him coach Mike McCarthy was benching him in favor of Mason Rudolph late Tuesday night, Nov. 24. Rodgers went on to say a lot of other explosive things about McCarthy, general manager Omar Khan and owner Art Rooney II over the course of his rambling 34-minute interview that captivated the NFL world. Required reading: T.J. Watt, Steelers defense make statement in first game without Aaron Rodgers You know the themes by now. Rodgers said McCarthy was sleeping in meetings and slacking on his film study. He called McCarthy unhealthy and unfit to be calling the offense for a team in the heat of a race for a playoff spot in the AFC. Et cetera, et cetera. It was noteworthy, then, when Freiermuth was one of the players to address the situation most directly in the locker room after his team cruised to a 27-5 victory against the Denver Broncos on Black Friday afternoon at Acrisure Stadium. “Pretty tough. I’m not going to lie. It was pretty tough,” he said when asked how he’s felt the past couple of days. “A lot of emotions. Just really, just sad. It was just a sad situation. We’ve just got to move on. Aaron’s still one of my closest friends, but we just have to continue to move on and keep winning.” Most of his teammates tried to stay away from it, obliquely referencing the difficulty of the preparation amid a national firestorm while trying to keep the focus on what happened on the field. That emotion was palpable, though. The room cleared out pretty quickly. Post-game victory music lasted maybe 10 minutes between the end of the game and media arriving for post-game interviews. Right tackle Brock Hoffman wasn’t even sure who’d received the game ball, if one was awarded. There were few hoots and fewer hollers. Not quite the scene you’d expect after what should have been a rousing home victory against one of the top teams in the conference. One the Steelers could see again in the postseason as they seek their first playoff win since 2016. “Prideful” was the word Freiermuth used to describe how he was feeling about the result. Earlier in the week, he’d delivered a fiery speech to the offense. He’s one of the unit’s most tenured players, with most of six seasons in Pittsburgh under his belt. He was glad to see his group respond with some explosive plays that complemented two defensive touchdowns in a game that was never really close. “I was feeling passionate about what was going on,” he said. “It was more from the heart of what the Steelers mean to me, and to my family and the Rooney family. And, just in general, nobody cares what we’re going through at all, so we’re either going to act soft about it or go out there and do something about it.” Hoffman found the comments “motivating” and felt they added energy to what was left of the short week of practice after the bombshell of the Rodgers news had landed, then settled. The team rallied around quarterback Mason Rudolph, who completed nine of his 15 passes for 142 yards and a touchdown with no interceptions in Rodgers’ place. The running game added 117 yards to control the clock. “Obviously, the whole world was laughing at us,” Hoffman said. “I’m not going to comment on that situation, but it felt like everybody was kind of counting us out. And for us to come in here, still stay undefeated at home and beat a really good Broncos team? You can’t write that any better.” A turning point this week was what coach Mike McCarthy called a “players council” meeting after Rodgers was benched, where many parties apparently spoke freely about what was and wasn’t working for the team that had been mired in a two-game losing streak against Cincinnati and Philadelphia. McCarthy had touted it as productive in responding to Rodgers’ comments, but few players really had their chance to tell their side of the story. Freiermuth said he appreciated it while implying, as Rodgers explicitly said in his interview, that some of it was overdue. “We were able to have grown conversations,” he said. “We were able to hold each other accountable and talk to each other about what we want to fix. Or what we can do better as a team, as players, as coaches. Really impressive about the conversations we’ve had this week. The asks, the wants that coaches and players see. And it was just great to put it together in a win and have those tough conversations. Because at the end of the day, when stuff happens and you talk it through, you’re able to get closer.” It’s therefore possible that these Steelers are fixable. They now sit at 7-4, a half-game behind the Bengals in the AFC North standings. Their schedule down the stretch is manageable. Jacksonville is the only remaining opponent with a winning record, so there’s a runway for this team to position itself well if it can continue to come together. Freiermuth pointedly stopped short of praising McCarthy, however, when asked how it felt to deliver a win for him personally. That felt noteworthy, given his proximity to Rodgers, and indicated that there’s probably quite a bit of healing still to come in a locker room that seems to lack buoyancy, even if the most recent result feels satisfying. “Obviously that’s tough for him and his family,” Freiermuth said of the criticism McCarthy has faced in the wake of Rodgers’ comments. “We just wanted to win in general.” This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Steelers locker room 'prideful' but muted after win amid Aaron Rodgers firestorm

The next one is really hard to get.” Ingrid Harbaugh started referring to the NFL as “Crazy Town” this year because of all the games decided by twists and turns in the final minutes. The three Thanksgiving Day games all featured game-winning scores in the final three seconds. The Eagles’ 21-point comeback against the Cowboys had the biggest impact on the NFC East-leading Giants — and serves as a great example of “Crazy Town.” New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh speaks at a press conference when the New York Giants practiced Wednesday, November 25, 2026 at Quest Diagnostics Training Center in East Rutherford, NJ. Robert Sabo for NY Post “Oh, my gosh, was it ever,” Harbaugh said. “It just goes to show you that these games are going to come down to the fourth quarter. You give the Eagles a lot of credit for the game they played. All six of those teams are fighting in the fourth quarter for the win. “Kind of goes to the other point … how hard it is to win these games. And, if you can, become a team that finds ways to win games and can keep their poise and make plays. Hopefully, you scheme some good plays up, too, to win games at the end. That’s the way they go. You have to be expecting that, I think — not be surprised by it.” Head coach John Harbaugh of the New York Giants is all smiles during the second half at MetLife Stadium, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026, in Brooklyn, NY. Could Carter’s workload be limited after his breakout 12-pressure game? “He seemed OK today,” Harbaugh said. “I’m sure we’ll be monitoring that, but he seemed good today. He seemed strong.” The Jameis Winston quarterback sneak package isn’t going anywhere. When the Giants benched Winston (after four starts) to go to J.J. McCarthy, they kept Winston involved by having him run the Tush Push and other versions of sneaks. “It was something he had been repping already, and so it was one less thing on J.J.’s plate,” Harbaugh said. “Just being honest, I’d probably say that was kind of where we started with it. We kind of got to the point where, if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it. It’s been good for us. It ends up being a whole package for us.”

stories.title: Inspired Steelers move on from Rodgers' exit with cathartic 27-5 win over sloppy Broncos
stories.summary: — The Pittsburgh Steelers weren't playing for embattled coach Mike McCarthy on Friday. They weren't necessarily playing for their season, either.
stories.detailText: PITTSBURGH -- — The Pittsburgh Steelers weren't playing for embattled coach Mike McCarthy on Friday. They weren't necessarily playing for their season, either. In some ways, it was larger than that. At the end of a chaotic week that saw quarterback Aaron Rodgers ' highly public departure thanks to an apparently long-simmering rift with McCarthy — a turn of events that former coach Mike Tomlin called a “dumpster fire” and threatened to turn one of the league's most stable franchises into a punchline — it felt on some level like “The Steeler Way” was at stake. Those left to navigate the fallout responded with a dominant 27-5 victory over the Denver Broncos that will turn down the volume, at least for a week. “Everything's in front of us,” McCarthy said at the end of one of the most challenging stretches of his 19 seasons as an NFL coach. Good thing, because the rearview mirror isn't a particularly pretty sight. It's one reason longtime defensive captain Cam Heyward and star outside linebacker T.J. Watt urged their teammates to “stay present” on a gloomy, rainy afternoon. “When tough times happen, they’re just right for us,” Heyward said. “We are built for this.” Well, maybe not quite this: their now-former future Hall of Fame quarterback going on national television eviscerating their coach, bringing issues normally kept in-house kicking and screaming into the light. Yet even while Rodgers was texting play-by-play announcer Al Michaels in the Amazon Prime broadcast booth, alleging the team banned him from the facility after benching him, the Steelers pushed around an AFC contender in a way that has been rare in recent years. Watt recovered a fumble by Bo Nix in the end zone for a touchdown, Jalen Ramsey intercepted Nix and returned it for a score, and Mason Rudolph played mistake-free football while taking over for Rodgers in yet another of his increasingly long list of starts made under difficult circumstances. Rudolph — who completed 9 of 15 passes for 142 yards, including a beautiful 22-yard touchdown toss to DK Metcalf — credited McCarthy for putting in the time to get him up to speed. “Proud of the way our team rallied around him and made it known that, like, ‘Dude, we’re behind you and let’s block out the noise, let’s go win a game,’” Rudolph said. Pittsburgh (7-4) ended Denver's six-game winning streak by harassing Nix into numerous mistakes in a steady rain, playing with the kind of energy that was lacking during losses to Cincinnati and Philadelphia that set the stage for Rodgers' stunning exit. “The situation happens, and it can go one or two ways,” Heyward said. “For our group to just strengthen and hold each other accountable and move forward, I think it’s huge.” That doesn't mean it was easy after Rodgers, who was highly popular in the locker room, called McCarthy's mental and physical fitness into question, creating a nearly unprecedented level of distraction. There was still the occasional No. 8 jersey in the Acrisure Stadium stands, and Metcalf appeared to give Rodgers a show of support after his third touchdown of the season, signing “stand on business, 8” — slang for sticking to your principles — in American Sign Language while celebrating in the end zone following his third touchdown of the season. “We obviously had a lot of stuff we had to filter through (in the) aftermath of his visit on national television,” Rudolph said. “So, just unfortunate. But we turn the page.” The Steelers did it by riding a defense that, when at its best, can be dominant. Nix gifted Pittsburgh an early touchdown when the ball slipped out of his hand on Denver's second possession and bounced into the end zone while he was pressured by Watt and Nick Herbig . Watt fell on it to send a jolt through the mist. Rudolph followed by directing a quick 85-yard drive, connecting with rookie Germie Bernard for a 58-yard catch-and-run, then lofted a back-shoulder fade to Metcalf that gave the Steelers their first 14-0 first-quarter lead since 2019. It was more than enough against the Broncos (8-3), who never really threatened to move into sole possession of first place in the AFC West after Kansas City lost at Buffalo on Thanksgiving night. Save for a second-quarter safety by linebacker Alex Singleton when he tackled running back Jaylen Warren in the Pittsburgh end zone, the Broncos mustered little on a day they managed just 205 yards while Nix took three sacks and tossed two picks. “I think early on, we gave them opportunities for momentum and that falls on me,” Denver coach Sean Payton said. “So, we can only lose the game once, but we got to learn from it and lick our wounds.” That's something the Steelers spent the 48 hours before kickoff doing. Pittsburgh found enough composure to win the first game of a difficult stretch that includes meetings with Houston and Jacksonville. It wasn't flashy, but for a team in crisis, it was enough. “Obviously the world’s kind of laughing at us in this situation,” guard Brock Hoffman said. “It felt like everybody was kind of counting us out and for us to come in here and still stay undefeated at home and beat a really good Broncos team, you can’t write that any better.” Injuries Broncos: WR Tony Franklin sustained a forearm injury in the first half. Steelers: CB Brandon Echols injured his quad covering a kickoff in the first quarter. ... OLB Jack Sawyer left late in the first quarter with a knee injury and did not return. Up next Broncos: Host Miami on Dec. 6. Steelers: Host Houston in primetime on Dec. 6. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here
