stories.title: 5 questions with a Chargers expert: What to expect from D.J. Uiagalelei?
stories.summary: We spoke with SB Nation’s Chargers blog about the upcoming Patriots opponent.
stories.detailText: On paper, the New England Patriots and Los Angeles Chargers are quite familiar with one another: they last met in January, in the wild card round of the NFL playoffs. However, there have been quite a few changes since that game, especially at the most important position on the field. Tommy DeVito will start at quarterback for New England in place of Drake Maye, while Justin Herbert’s absence as Chargers QB will allow D.J. Uiagalelei to get his first career start. To learn more about him, and the rest of the Chargers in 2026, we spoke with Michael Peterson of Pats Pulpit’s sister site Bolts From the Blue , the SB Nation community for all things Chargers. 1. With Justin Herbert missing this game due to a concussion, what can you tell us about backup D.J. Uiagalelei’s strengths and weaknesses? So D.J. Uiagalelei has made massive strides since coming out of college. The fact he has been able to stay with a NFL team this long is truly a testament to that because he was — to put it bluntly — a horrendous passer to end his collegiate career. With a full year and more behind Herbert, mainly as the third-stringer, he’s progressed enough to be a serviceable player for an emergency situation like this. As a passer, he is fairly composed in the pocket and has enough athleticism to escape and extend plays. He also plays with some notable confidence and will not think twice about attempting a tough throw. However, he’s not reckless with the football. He knows when to pull it down and get yards on the ground when possible. In his first NFL action in garbage time against the Texans, he helped bring the offense down the field and even threw his first professional touchdown on a great rip over the middle. His biggest weakness will be that he’s still a wildcard and an unknown in this league. He could be serviceable like I mentioned, but he could also flail in the moment like most young passers in their first career starts. I think Mike Vrabel would be wise to turn up the heat early and often and hope the second-year UDFA crumbles under the pressure. 2. Why has it taken so long for Omarion Hampton to start breaking out, and what challenges does he present for a defense? Hampton unfortunately did not help himself this year by beginning the campaign with back-to-back games where he lost a fumble. It also did not help that he lost those fumbles in pivotal moments that directly led to the Chargers losing said games. It unfortunately took a bit for him to get back into the god graces of Mike McDaniel and now he seems to be off and running with a renewed energy. He’s been phenomenal and looks every bit the player the Chargers wanted to take in the first round. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . As a runner, Hampton’s skillset is not designed to make someone miss by being shifty. He’s going to make them miss by running full speed through the weak point of your tackle attempt to consistently gain extra yards and fall forward at the end of runs. He’s the type of runner that will get the most out of the minor creases given to him and when the defense is worn down by the fourth quarter, he’ll look to keep pounding it even more. Patriots should come prepared to try and get him stopped before his momentum builds, not unlike how the Chargers kept Derrick Henry in check during their lone win of the season. 3. LT Joe Alt is a Pro Bowler, but the rest of the Chargers’ offensive line consists of rookies and backups. Where are the non-Alt bright spots up front, and who do you expect the Patriots to try to exploit? One guy who went from roster afterthought to solid starter the past few weeks has been rookie left guard Logan Taylor. He was a sixth-round pick out of Boston College this year and mainly was used at tackle during the preseason despite guard be the obvious place for him in the NFL. Once he settled in after being forced into the starting lineup, he’s been one of the lone bright spots outside of Alt. Another recent bright spot has also been the return of Kayode Awosika who, after being the original starter at left guard before his fibula injury, is now starting at right guard over Cole Strange (who should have been benched a long time ago). Both of the guard spots being reinforced has led to back-to-back strong rushing games for Hampton, as well as two consecutive intereption-less games by Herbert. As far as which player up front the Patriots should exploit, it has to be rookie right tackle Travis Burke. As good as Burke has been in the run game, he is quite a bit behind as far as pass protection fundamentals. He is athletic enough to stay outside, but he lacks proper set points and punch mechanics. He gets beat by twitchier rushers and overall speed that can threaten his corner more than he likes. He is coming off a horrible game against David Bailey and the Jets and the Patriots should do their best to exploit that side of the line this week. 4. What has contributed to the Chargers’ struggles stopping opposing passing games? Are there any defenders the Patriots should try to avoid? Against the Jets, the absence of cornerback Tarheeb Still was felt, especially when injuries have continued to rear their head in a position group that is terribly shallow. Undrafted rookie Rodney Shelley has played a lot this season and his production has been abysmal. Even veteran Donte Jackson, who has battled multiple injuries this year, is still very feast-or-famine. The absence of Derwin James has also been apparent. He’s a back-to-back second-team All-Pro slot defender and anyone who knows ball understands how good an elite slot player can be for a defense. The Chargers have been getting by — for the most part — with a group of guys no one has probably heard of at the second and third levels. The Jets game was a bit of a fluke, but they’ll have to right the ship fast to avoid making that result less of “who they are” and more of that fluke I just mentioned. 5. It seems there is some disconnect between Jim Harbaugh, Mike McDaniel, and Justin Herbert. What is happening with the Chargers’ current leadership structure, and who do you see remaining in L.A. when the dust settles? What some may not understand about Harbaugh’s role as the head coach is that he is a true CEO. He does not have a hand in helping scheme either side of the ball. He makes his hires and then he allows how coaches to coach. That’s a major reason why no coordinator has been fired or changed during the season under his leadership and it’s the main reason why McDaniel was never going to be fired. There’s no one to pick up the slack and Harbaugh sure wasn’t going to step in and start calling plays for the first time in decades. When it’s all said and done, Harbaugh will most likely remain, even if he truly should not. The team will owe him a ton of money over the next two years and the Spanos family will not want to fork out money to a coach that’s no longer working for him. Harbaugh’s two 11-win seasons prior to this year still gives him some grace, but with how bad this year is, there will be no more grace for him should this disaster continue into the 2027 season.

stories.detailText: Quarterback Sam Darnold is back as Seattle's starter this week, after missing two games due to quad and rib injuries. It's an opportunity to improve on what has been a challenging start to the 2026 season. On Friday, coach Mike Macdonald was asked to assess Darnold's performance when healthy. "I think he’s done a good job," Macdonald said. "As a football team, we’ve been good enough to go 6-4, and we want to get better. Yeah, he’s right there with everybody else.” Well, he's not right there with the player who replaced him. Drew Lock has started three games and played all but one drive of another. His record is 4-0. Darnold is 2-4. And their numbers are starkly different. Darnold has thrown 10 touchdown passes and nine interceptions. Lock has thrown seven touchdown passes and no interceptions. Lock's passer rating is 125.6. Darnold's is 79.5. Lock's games have come against the Patriots, the Cardinals twice, and the Raiders. Darnold has faced the Commanders, Chargers, 49ers, Broncos, Chiefs, and Bears — a much tougher slate of opponents. The Seahawks won a Super Bowl with Darnold. That counts for something. Still, they're 6-4. They have an opportunity to get a seventh win on Sunday, with Brock Purdy out for the game against the 49ers.

stories.title: Mike McCarthy just 'focused on winning' after Aaron Rodgers saga
stories.summary: Mike McCarthy kept his focus on winning after helping guide the Steelers to a "Black Friday" victory following Aaron Rodgers' unceremonious departure.
stories.detailText: Mike McCarthy helped guide the Pittsburgh Steelers to a resounding 27-5 victory over the Denver Broncos on "Black Friday" after one of the franchise's most tumultuous weeks in recent memory. The trouble began after the Steelers announced veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers was being benched in favor of Mason Rudolph at 11:10 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Nov. 24. The following day, Rodgers did not report to the Steelers' facility and instead aired his grievances with McCarthy in an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" before Pittsburgh released the 42-year-old quarterback . The accusations claimed McCarthy had fallen asleep in team meetings and had performed a "1, 2, 3, Packers!" during a halftime huddle breakdown with his team, among other issues. Naturally, it garnered significant attention in the NFL world, with many decrying Rodgers for breaking the sanctity of his team's locker-room bond. And one of the most notable reactions came from McCarthy's predecessor, Mike Tomlin, who referred to the organization as having a "dumpster fire" on its hands following Rodgers' release. Following the Steelers' Week 12 win, McCarthy was asked for his reaction to those comments. "I really don't have one," he replied , stoically, during his postgame news conference. "Let's just be real here. There's only so much time and energy in the day. I think you have to, when you go through things like that, I have to put all my energy into winning." "I get that this is part of the responsibility and the opinions and comments of others is why I'm in here to answer questions," McCarthy added. "But I'm focused on winning." McCarthy's approach paid off, as the Steelers were able to improve to 7-4 with their victory over the Broncos. That has put them a half-a-game behind the Cincinnati Bengals in the AFC North race while giving them more breathing room in the wild-card race, as they now are a game-and-a-half ahead of the No. 8 seed New England Patriots. McCarthy appreciated earning that victory after what he acknowledged was a difficult week for his team. "It was definitely a hard travel week for us as a football team," he said. "I'm proud of our players, I'm proud of our coaching staff, I'm proud of our support staff and I really appreciate all the other support." The Steelers were playing at home at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh in Week 12, so it wasn't immediately clear whether McCarthy was using the phrase "hard travel week" metaphorically as a reference to a series of events the team endured amid the Rodgers saga. Either way, McCarthy came out of the win pleased with his team. He praised Rudolph for being able to effectively guide the team without Rodgers and also praised his veteran-laden defense for its stalwart performance against Bo Nix. But above all else, McCarthy was grateful for the team's veteran leadership for establishing "urgency" after a meeting they held earlier in the week. "I think it says a tremendous amount about the team," McCarthy said, referencing the win. "I really probably want to pivot off the leadership council meeting. Everything that was discussed was healthy. A lot of things in there, but what came out of it was urgency. And I thought our leaders did a tremendous job of bringing the urgency to their rooms and it definitely showed up." "You definitely saw the urgency today," McCarthy later added. "That's what really stood out for me as far as the vibe in the locker room. Our guys do a good job of that. From the get-go, our leaders really had the guys going. And our defense got us started. We played the game that we needed to play. Just very, very impressed and very proud of the way we handled this." stories.title: DJ Uiagalelei to start for Chargers with Justin Herbert in concussion protocol
stories.summary: Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert was ruled out for Sunday as he remains in concussion protocol, coach Jim Harbaugh said Friday, meaning DJ Uiagalelei will start against Tommy DeVito and the Patriots.
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES -- Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert was ruled out for Sunday's game against the New England Patriots as he remains in concussion protocol, coach Jim Harbaugh said Friday. So what was once scheduled as a primetime showdown between Herbert and Drake Maye will now be DJ Uiagalelei vs. Tommy DeVito at SoFi Stadium (CBS, 4:05 p.m. ET). Harbaugh announced Uiagalelei as the team's starter Friday, with No. 2 option Trey Lance (groin) on injured reserve. The Chargers (1-9) also signed quarterback Jake Browning to their 53-man roster from their practice squad Thursday to serve as Uiagalelei's backup. Herbert played all 60 offensive snaps in the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets last Sunday, but didn't take part in postgame interviews, with a team spokesperson saying at the time that he was in concussion protocol. Meanwhile, the Patriots (5-5) have spent the past two weeks preparing for an extended stretch without Maye, who fractured his right fibula in the first quarter of a Week 10 loss to the Lions in Munich, and are coming off their bye in Week 11. Two days after Maye's injury, the NFL flexed the Patriots-Chargers game out of its Sunday night slot in favor of Raiders - Browns . Uiagalelei, 25, entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2025 after five collegiate seasons at Clemson , Oregon State and Florida State , and he spent 2025 on the Chargers' practice squad. He began 2026 on the Chargers' practice squad as well before getting signed to the 53-man roster when Lance went on IR in October. Sunday will mark his first career NFL start after he made his regular-season debut in relief in Week 9, which included throwing a touchdown pass. "I've seen a lot of growth from DJ," Harbaugh said earlier this week. "He was already a very talented player, but every part of the game, it's something a quarterback is constantly working on -- there's so many things to get better at at that position." Patriots coach Mike Vrabel acknowledged Friday how the team was preparing for multiple possibilities at quarterback, with the primary focus on the Chargers' scheme. "We can go back and watch the 173 snaps that DJ's had the last two years in preseason and some of the regular season ... but the plays are the plays; what they do is what they do," he said. "I'm sure they'll have some modifications, and we'll just have to see how the game plays out. But we'll have to make sure that we're good against the run no matter who the quarterback is; it's what they've done well lately, and that'll be a good place to start."

stories.detailText: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks have released their final injury report for their crucial Week 12 showdown with the San Francisco 49ers. While the 49ers won’t have quarterback Brock Purdy due to an ankle injury , the Seahawks will get Sam Darnold back from his rib and quad injuries suffered back in their Week 8 loss to the Chicago Bears. Darnold was a full participant in practice all week and has no game designation. As expected, right tackle Abe Lucas (ankle) and left guard Quenton Nelson (knee) are both out. Mike Macdonald announced they would miss the 49ers game with their respective injuries earlier in the week, so there’s nothing new on that front. The only other player ruled a no-go for Sunday is defensive tackle Jarran Reed, who played through a toe injury against the Las Vegas Raiders but didn’t practice all of this week. It’ll once again mean more snaps for Rylie Mills on the interior defensive line, and perhaps a few more looks for Brandon Pili at nose tackle. All things considered, Seattle’s injury report is very positive. Leonard Williams (stinger) and Charles Cross (ankle) are back, while any worries about the lengthy list of players on the report can be put to rest due to the number of full Friday participants. stories.title: Steelers rally after tumultuous week to grab key Black Friday win over Broncos
stories.summary: The Steelers scored two defensive touchdowns and flustered Broncos QB Bo Nix throughout to rally to a key Black Friday victory.
stories.detailText: PITTSBURGH -- After an emotionally fraught and turbulent week, the Pittsburgh Steelers found a way to turn the page from one of the most chaotic chapters in the organization's history in a 27-5 win against the Denver Broncos at Acrisure Stadium. The Steelers led wire-to-wire in the upset win, alleviating the tension around the organization and the entire fan base after a week that began with wide receiver DK Metcalf coming under fire for being ejected in a Week 11 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles and ended with Mike McCarthy defending his decision to bench quarterback Aaron Rodgers and his own fitness to be the Steelers' head coach. The win didn't just boost the team's vibes. It also strengthened their odds to make the playoffs. Entering the game in possession of the final wild-card spot, the Steelers now have a 92% chance to make it to the playoffs, according to ESPN Analytics. Here are the most important things to know for both teams: Pittsburgh Steelers (7-4) What to make of QB performance : The decision to bench Rodgers stemmed from the ultimatum issued by the quarterback to the head coach to change playcalling, but it was also done with the hope that Rudolph could provide a spark. He did that Friday, beginning with the roar from the crowd at Acrisure Stadium when Mason Rudolph stepped on the field for the first snap just after 3 p.m. ET. The career backup played efficient football in his first start since Rodgers was sidelined with a broken wrist in Week 12 last season against Chicago. Not only did Rudolph complete his first five attempts for 94 yards, but he also hit rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard for a 58-yard catch-and-run that set up for a 22-yard touchdown throw to Metcalf a few plays later. Most surprising performance : Jalen Ramsey . The veteran defensive back has had several splash, impact plays this season, but he put together one of his most complete games in a Steelers uniform on Friday. Ramsey picked off a badly thrown ball by quarterback Bo Nix and returned it for a touchdown just before halftime to give the Steelers a 24-5 lead at the break. The score marked Ramsey's second career pick-six -- his first came as a rookie in 2016. Ramsey came up big again in the second half, putting an exclamation point on the third quarter with a pass breakup on third down to force the Broncos to settle for a 53-yard field goal attempt -- which Wil Lutz missed. Stat to know : With the help of two defensive touchdowns, the Steelers led the Broncos 24-5 at the half. The last time an Aaron Rodgers-quarterbacked team had 24-plus points in the first half was in Week 17 of the 2022 season, when he was still on the Green Bay Packers (they led the Minnesota Vikings 27-3). Rudolph has done it twice since then, including Friday. -- Brooke Pryor Next game: vs. Houston Texans (Dec. 6, 8:20 p.m. ET) Denver Broncos (8-3) On a rain-soaked Friday afternoon against a team engulfed in its own drama, the Broncos looked like the team in disarray in a lopsided loss to the Steelers. And the Broncos' résumé as a heavyweight in the AFC's playoff race is now a little soggy. The Steelers started Rudolph at quarterback after Rodgers' public takedown of the organization this past week -- Rudolph's first start of the year -- and yet it was the Broncos who looked overwhelmed as two Nix turnovers resulted in Steelers touchdowns, which was plenty for Pittsburgh. Most concerning for the Broncos, beyond Nix's struggles in an almost constant near-freezing rain, was this was just the kind of weather, crowd noise and road game scenario the Broncos could see in the playoffs. Their offense did not look nearly up to the challenge at all. Now at 8-3 overall and 3-3 on the road, the Broncos have let an immense opportunity to pass the Kansas City Chiefs in the AFC West slip away for the moment. Instead, they have put themselves in a fight of their own making. Denver is also two games behind the Buffalo Bills for the AFC's top seed. But the Broncos have their work cut out to have any postseason home games come January. Most surprising performance : The defense didn't have a bad day -- though Germie Bernard 's 58-yard catch-and-run in the first half and a 37-yard catch by Roman Wilson in the fourth quarter joined the growing list of big plays it has surrendered -- but Rudolph was far more efficient than expected. The Steelers' former backup had one completion for 2 yards this season before Friday but was comfortable enough in the pocket to throw a 22-yard touchdown pass to Metcalf in the first quarter ... over Pat Surtain II no less. The Broncos pressured Rudolph at times and sacked him once, but for an offense said to be in chaos, the Broncos didn't make Rudolph nearly uncomfortable enough. What to make of QB performance : Where to start? Nix's unforced fumble at the Broncos' 6-yard line was recovered in the end zone for the Steelers' first touchdown of the game, and he threw an interception that was returned for a touchdown just before halftime. Yes, the conditions made it a tough ask, but Nix struggled mightily to find any rhythm in a balky bad weather outing, reminiscent of a 12-of-25 day he had against the Jets in MetLife Stadium as a rookie. It was the seventh game of his career with at least two interceptions and his first of this season, as Nix finished 22-of-40 for 169 yards and the two interceptions. Trend to watch : Some of the Broncos' biggest contracts are on the offensive line, but Friday was the ninth time this season that the Broncos rushed for fewer than 4 yards per carry in a game and the third they've rushed for 3 or fewer yards per carry. On a day when they desperately needed a run game to pull through against one of the league's best run defenses, rookie running back Jonah Coleman wasn't as decisive as he has been so far this season and the Broncos were unable to create enough gaps to get him free. - Jeff Legwold . Next game: vs. Miami Dolphins (Dec. 6, 4:05 p.m. ET)

stories.title: SCORIGAMI: The NFL’s list of unique scores has added more in 2026
stories.summary: The NFL’s crazy scoring has led to a bunch of unique final scores recently. We got our latest one in 2026.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images There had been 1095 unique final scores in NFL history as of the conclusion of the 2025 season. We are now up to 1102 with the ones added during 2026. With teams scoring more points in games, the extra point moving out to a 33-yard kick, and teams deciding to go for two more often to gain edges, never-before-seen final scores are still happening despite the NFL playing for more than 100 years. These unique scores are also called “Scorigami”. Many of the Scorigami we are seeing are for 40-plus point games that have high scoring from both teams, but we’ve also been seeing scores in the 30s that have never happened. It’s not just high scores that have never happened, though. A game has never finished in a 2-2 tie, for instance. The NFL didn’t allow two-point conversions until 1994, and we’ve never seen an 8-7 game. A game has never ended in a 9-9 tie, among other scores still out there. How may Scorigamis can we expect in 2026? Since 1992, there have been three or more Scoigamis in every season. The average since the start of the 2000 season is seven per year with the high of 14 in 2013 and a low of three in 2022 and 2009. NFL Scorigami games in 2026 The 2026 NFL season didn’t wait to get the Scorigami train rolling. Two NFC North teams won games on the Sunday of opening weekend with scores that had never happened before. They were the 1096th and 1097th unique scores in NFL history. Bears beat Panthers 59-37 in Week 1 Normally when we get a Scorigami, it’s because something weird happened in the game. This one wasn’t that. The Bears just laid the smack down. Chicago scored 14 points in the first, third, and fourth quarters along with a 17-point third quarter. All of those are regular scores, there were just a lot of them. We had a late extra point blocked, but 59-38 also has never happened. Vikings defeat Packers 39-22 in Week 1 The Packers missed an extra point in the first quarter, but that didn’t trigger a whole lot of unique scores on its own. Everything stayed pretty normal until the fourth quarter when Minnesota scored to take the lead. They converted a 2-point conversion to go up 25-22. Scoring 25 points in an NFL game is weird. Then Minnesota added two more 7-point touchdowns on top of it. A 39-point day is pretty rare. (A 32-22 score has also never happened.) Bengals defeat Titans 43-36 in Week 8 After a two-point conversion made the score a very normal 21-21, things got weird. A Bengals safety made it 23-21. The Bengals couldn’t get a two-point conversion on a later touchdown after the Titans scored, making it 29-28. Then the Titans got a two-point on their next score to make it a seven-point lead at 36-29. The Bengals scored and kicked an extra point and the game sat at 36-36 at the end of regulation. It should be noted that an overtime touchdown would have won the game without an extra point before this season and 42-36 has happened before. 49ers defeat Cowboys 46-40 in Week 10 The Cowboys didn’t get the extra point after scoring a touchdown, which made it 16-10 in the second quarter. In the fourth quarter, the score was 38-19 when the Cowboys got in the end zone and tried to make it an 11-point game but failed at 38-25. That’s when things got weirder. Dallas made it 38-32 then the 49ers scored a long touchdown with a 2-point conversion to get the to the very strange 46 points. 46-32 was a Scorigami, as was 46-39, but the Cowboys went for 2 after their last TD and got it to 46-40. Also a Scorigami. Bengals defeat Steelers 38-18 in Week 10 For the second time on the same day, we saw a Scorigami. And it was the Bengals’ second in three weeks. With the Bengals up 31-2, the Steelers scored and went for two to make it 31-11. it’s weird because it’s still a three-touchdown game and doesn’t really help him close the gap but whatever. While 31-11 would have been Scorigami, both teams scored again to make it 38-18. The only 38-point Scorigami winners left now are 38-2 and 38-4. Cowboys defeat Titans 51-20 in Week 11 For the second straight week, the Dallas Cowboys were part of a Scorigami and the Titans get on the board for the second time in 2026. Dallas seems to have the formula — score a ton of points. There are a ton of 51-point games that have not hit in the history of the NFL. Down 51-23, the Titans scored with 31 seconds left. 51-23 and 51-29 have both happened before as has 51-31. The Titans kicking the extra point to make is 51-30 was the difference. Steelers defeat Broncos 27-5 in Week 12 The 27 points is normal, but 5 points is not. A safety and a field goal were all the Broncos could muster on Black Friday. A lot of other scores have happened against 5 points, but not 27. When the Steelers added a fourth-quarter field goal for the only points of the second half, it moved from 24-5 (which has happened once before) to 27-5, which has never happened. Scorigami. Some potential Scorigami numbers to watch for in 2026 8-7: Someone scores a late touchdown and goes for the win, not the tie 9-9: Two struggling offenses end in a 9-9 tie, or a 6-6 game at end of regulation ending this way 18-8: Feels like it should be taken 25-18: A few ways to get to 18 then a score to win 32-22: A team playing catch up gets to 22 and a team keeping them away gets to 32 41-41: With 40-40 off the board, lets go one more 42-25: A team up late pushes it to a three-possession game 46-17: It’s the lowest number against the very common 17 47-40: let’s score a ton of points 50-0: The cleanest shutout number 50-3: It’s the lowest number against the very common 3 60-14: It’s the lowest number against the very common 14 How each NFL Scorigami in 2025 happened After seven Scorigamis in 2024, there were four NFL games to hit new finals in 2025, two including the high-scoring Buffalo Bills. here is how each of them got there in chronological order: Bills beat Ravens 41-40 in Week 1 This game features two high-powered offenses at the height of their powers, but the Bills started going for two in the third quarter and missed on consecutive attempts. Halfway through the fourth quarter, they sat at 25 points, a rare number. A missed extra point by the Ravens put Baltimore at 40 — not an entirely uncommon number on its own — before the Bills’ final push. Buffalo made it 40-38 after two touchdowns and an extra point but failed to convert on the game-tying two-point conversion. They got the ball back and kicked a field goal as time expired to win 41-40. Cowboys and Packers tie 40-40 in Week 4 There are several ties still available on this list, but not as many as you would think. The NFL didn’t have sudden death overtime until 1974 when they added a 15-minute frame, so there were a bunch of ties prior to 1974 but then a lot fewer. They modified the rule in 2010 so it wasn’t sudden death for a first-drive field goal then shortened the time to 10 minutes in 2017. In 2025, they gave every team a possession. With those recent changes, ties can be more common. Those rule changes directly impacted this game between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers. Dallas didn’t win after their first-possession field goal because Green Bay was guaranteed a possession. The Packers only had 4:40 on the clock and drove deep into Dallas territory. After shots to the end zone failed, they settled for a 40-40 tie as time expired. Texans beat Jaguars 36-29 in Week 10 In the third quarter, the Jaguars were up 23-10 and scored another touchdown. Up 19, they knew the Texans had to score three times to win so they tried to make it a 21-point lead to make it three touchdowns to tie or win. That play failed, and they sat at 29 points with a 19-point lead. The Texans then scored a touchdown plus a two-point conversion to make it an 11-point game. Another touchdown with a failed two-point conversion made it a 5-point game. Houston scored again to go up 30-29 and tried another two-point conversion to ensure a late field goal wouldn’t beat them, but that try failed with 31 seconds on the clock. Here’s where things get nuts. A 30-29 score has happened before. But the Texans returned a fumble for a touchdown to make it 36-29 as time expired. A final of 37-29 and 38-29 has happened, but because there was no time on the clock, there was no extra point attempt, and the final stood at Scorigami. Bills beat Buccaneers 44-32 in Week 11 For Buffalo’s second Scorigami of the year, they also topped 40 points. The Buccaneers started the shenanigans in the third quarter when they scored a touchdown to make it 26-21. They went for two to try and make it 28-21 but the conversion failed. Buffalo got to 31 the old-fashioned way, with four touchdowns and PATs plus a field goal, and the score was 31-26. After another touchdown, the Bucs tried to make it a three-point lead with another two-point conversion that failed, sticking them at 32 points. Buffalo scored another touchdown to make it 37-32 and failed the two-point conversion to try and make it a seven-point game. The Bills’ final touchdown game them a 43-32 lead and Buffalo pushed it to 44-32 with an extra point to make it a two-touchdown lead with 2:35 left.

stories.title: The Steelers vs Broncos final score has never happened in NFL history
stories.summary: The Steelers vs Broncos final score has never happened in NFL history.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Just a couple weeks ago, the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals finished with a final score that had never happened before in NFL history . Now 12 days later, the Steelers are at it again. The 27-5 final is the 1102nd different final score in an NFL game. When we get a new final score in the NFL, it’s called Scorigami . Normally when we get a Scorigami it’s because a team scores an absolute boatload of points and often something weird happens, usually with two-point conversions. We got a safety and not much else from the Broncos on Friday, resulting in this Scorigami. I don’t need to tell you this was a strange game with all the defensive scores, but the biggest one for our purposes was the Broncos’ safety. It was a pedestrian 14-0 when Jaylen Warren was tackled in the end zone, leading to a 14-2 score. The Broncos scored next on a field goal, to make it 5 points on the board. A 14-5 final has happened, as has 17-5, and 24-5. It wasn’t until the Steelers put the 27 on the board that we got a unique score of 27-5. If Denver had made their field goal, 27-8 was also a Scorigami. 2026 NFL Scorigamis This is the seventh Scorigami of the 2026 NFL season. September 13: Chicago Bears 59, Carolina Panthers 37 September 13: Minnesota Vikings 39, Green Bay Packers 22 November 1: Cincinnati Bengals 43, Tennessee Titans 36 November 15: San Francisco 49ers 46, Dallas Cowboys 40 November 15: Cincinnati Bengals 38, Pittsburgh Steelers 18 November 22: Dallas Cowboys 51, Tennessee Titans 30 November 27: Pittsburgh Steelers 27, Denver Broncos 5 During the 2025 season we saw four Scorigamis: Bills beat Buccaneers 44-32 Bills beat Ravens 41-40 Cowboys and Packers tie 40-40 Texans beat Jaguars 36-29

stories.title: Brock Purdy receives major injury update ahead of 49ers-Seahawks game
stories.summary: The 49ers will be without Brock Purdy on Sunday against the Seahawks due to an ankle injury.
stories.detailText: The 49ers won’t have quarterback Brock Purdy when they take on the Seahawks on Sunday. Purdy is dealing with an ankle injury suffered during last week’s game against the Vikings and Mac Jones will start in his place, coach Kyle Shanahan announced Friday. San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy reacts before an NFL football game against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AFP via Getty Images Kyle Shanahan has announced Mac Jones will start against the Seahawks. pic.twitter.com/nBHcZtzUSW — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) November 27, 2026 Purdy sustained the injury in the second quarter of last week’s 35-10 victory over the Vikings in Mexico City. He had his ankles taped for the second half before he finished 21-of-26 passing for 255 yards and three touchdowns while helping solidify his case as an MVP candidate. Shanahan told reporters it was a mid-ankle sprain that didn’t heal as quickly as the team would have hoped. Purdy missed practice the entire week, leaving Jones to receive practice reps with the starters. “Any time it’s not a high ankle sprain, you get pretty relieved. But it was more mid than low, which is a little bit worse,” Shanahan said. “(I) kinda had a feeling just the way it was by the time Wednesday came around. So didn’t heal up as fast as we wanted so we had to shut him down.” Shanahan was asked if Purdy would be available for the following game when the 49ers travel to play the Giants. He said it was too soon to tell. “But I’m pretty optimistic about it. But I was about this week to start, and then it changes. Hopefully it’ll be all right,” he said. The 49ers signed Jones before the 2025 season to a two-year, $8.4 million contract to upgrade their backup quarterback situation after struggling through stints with Brandon Allen and Joshua Dobbs the season prior. “Mac’s been awesome,” Shanahan said. “He’s had a great week. We went through this a lot last year, so we got a ton of confidence in Mac. Mac’s had a hell of a camp, and he’s the same guy every day. So it’s been a good week with Mac.” Mac Jones #10 of the San Francisco 49ers attempts a pass against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Getty Images The 49ers believe Jones is one of the NFL’s best backup quarterbacks after relying on him heavily when Purdy was injured in 2025. Teams called about acquiring Jones at the trade deadline, but the price was reportedly too high. The Vikings were reportedly among those teams and instead opted to swap a third-round draft pick with the Raiders for Kirk Cousins. “Any time you have a backup quarterback you believe could be one of the better starters in this league, that’s a hell of a deal,” Shanahan said. “It’s always hard and tempting when someone offers a lot of stuff, because you know how much that can help your team. But you’re kinda glad you don’t have to make that decision if because of how bad it is if your starter gets hurt and you’re missing that guy. So really grateful that he’s here and that we didn’t make that trade.” San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy listens to a question after an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys in Arlington, Texas, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. AP Photo/Julio Cortez San Francisco went 5-3 in Jones’ eight starts last season while Purdy was dealing with a turf toe injury suffered in Week 1. Jones completed 69.6% of his passes, averaging 269 yards per game with 13 touchdown passes and six interceptions. Jones kept the 49ers afloat while they finished 12-5 and made the playoffs. Sunday’s game will mark the 11th Purdy has missed due to injury since the start of the 2024 season.

teamStories.summary: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers is questionable for Sunday night's game at Cleveland because of an ankle injury he suffered in Week 10. Las Vegas will also be missing two of its starting defensive tackles and a backup.
teamStories.detailText: HENDERSON, Nev. -- Brock Bowers ' status for the Las Vegas Raiders ' matchup against the Cleveland Browns is uncertain, as the All-Pro tight end is questionable to play Sunday night because of an ankle injury. Bowers missed practice Friday after being limited Wednesday and Thursday. Coach Klint Kubiak didn't say whether Bowers' absence was a scheduled rest day to get him healthier for the Week 12 contest. "We're doing everything we can to get him ready for the game," Kubiak said. Kubiak didn't elaborate on whether the team will conduct a pregame workout for Bowers, or if the star pass catcher had any setbacks while recovering from the injury, which happened on the Raiders' opening drive in Week 10 and kept him out of last week's game against Denver . Bowers began the practice week without tape on his right ankle. On Thursday, his ankle was heavily taped up, and he was not seen on the practice field Friday. "He's working through what works for him," Kubiak said. "What makes him feel the best and what he can play his best at, whether it's with or without the tape." Kubiak reiterated that the team's upcoming Week 13 bye week will not factor into the decision to play Bowers on Sunday. If healthy, he will suit up. In other injury news, right guard and 2024 second-round pick Jackson Powers-Johnson sustained an Achilles injury during Friday's practice. Powers-Johnson appeared in 10 games, making four starts before losing the starting job to rookie Trey Zuhn III . Las Vegas will also be without three defensive tackles against the Browns. Starters Tonka Hemingway (stinger) and Adam Butler (concussion) and backup Tim Keenan III have been ruled out. Second-year defensive lineman JJ Pegues (elbow) is questionable but was a full participant each practice day this week. Thomas Booker IV and Folorunso Fatukasi are the only healthy defensive tackles on the active roster. Edge rusher Kwity Paye can line up in the interior if needed. Practice squad defensive tackles Chris Williams , Brandon Cleveland and David Blay Jr. have an opportunity to be elevated ahead of Sunday's game. Williams played 24 defensive snaps against Denver. The injuries up front aren't a good sign for the Raiders, who have lacked consistent production from their interior defensive line. Las Vegas is 32nd in rushing yards allowed (149.5) and 30th in run-stop win rate by interior linemen (24.9%).

teamStories.title: Raiders Week 12: Schwesinger, Browns defense an active and aggressive group
teamStories.summary: Klint Kubiak will need to dial up man coverage beaters for rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza in Sunday Night clash
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images What’s the next step for Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza? “Winning,” head coach Klint Kubiak was quick to say when asked that very question during his media availability earlier this week. A question later, however, the rookie head coach added much-needed context when it comes to his prized No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, when asked about Mendoza’s performance in his first two initial starts. “I think we just conveyed it to the whole team. And how did he respond? He’s played two solid football games, and he’s got to keep improving,” Kubiak said. “But we’re not putting it all on him. It’s a team game and he’ll play better when the whole team plays better.” A collective effort from the the 4-7 Raiders where complementary football is present throughout and not fleeting is a must for Las Vegas this coming Sunday against the 6-4 Cleveland Browns. The host Browns are unbeaten at home (4-0) and are trying to keep pace of the AFC North-leading Cincinnati Bengals (7-3 overall) and staying ahead of the ragga muffin Pittsburgh Steelers (also 6-4). While head coach Todd Monken’s Cleveland offense is near the bottom of the league rankings — 27th in points scored at 188 total; 21st in yards gained at 3,149 — his chosen defensive coordinator, Mike Rutenberg, has the Browns defense in the middle ranked 14th in both points allowed (220) and yards yielded (3,274). While that may be a far cry from the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos defense Mendoza faced in his two initial starts, Rutenberg’s Dawg Pound defense is an aggressive man-based group, which will test the Raiders rookie. #Browns Carson Schwesinger is the only LB currently in the NFL with -100+ tackles -3 sacks -3 Forced Fumbles Doesn’t matter where on the field you are. If you have the ball Carson will find you pic.twitter.com/kzGabdYeUI — Mac🦬 (@tha_buffalo) November 20, 2026 The heart of Cleveland’s defense is Carson Schwesinger, a 23-year-old linebacker who arrived on the NFL scene as a second-round pick (33rd overall) out of UCLA. A special teams maniac that transformed into a true starter with the Bruins, the 6-foot-3 and 242-pounder from California won the 2025 AP NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year award last season and is once again playing with his hair on fire in Year 2. Able to do it all — stop the run, blitz, tackle, and cover — Schwesinger was one of my popular mock draft picks to the Raiders and it’s easy to see why. He’s racked up 102 total tackles with six stops for loss, three sacks, four quarterback hits, a pass deflection, and three forced fumbles so far this season. With Schwesinger in the middle of the defense with the green dot helmet, he relays the play calls from Rutenberg and ensures the Cleveland defense is lined up and makes adjustments. And the middle linebackers athleticism and high football IQ allowed the defensive coordinator to go from a heavy zone defense to a heavy man-press scheme that’d make legendary Raiders owner Al Davis proud. According to ESPN Next Gen stats, the Browns ran man coverage concepts on about 45 percent of its defensive snaps (one of highest marks in the league) with a 64 percent press rate and 74 percent single-high safety alignment. This has allowed defensive tackle Mason Graham and defensive end Isaiah McGuire to each rack up four sacks alongside nine and six tackles for loss, respectively. And behind them are defensive tackles Maliek Collins and Adin Hunington racking up 3.5 sacks, each. Cornerbacks Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell, often left on an island in the press-man scheme, are stifling cover men with Ward leading the team with three interceptions and 12 pass deflections while Campbell has one pick and six pass deflections. Thus, it’d be wise for Kubiak and his coaching staff to hone in on man-beater concepts and Mendoza executing the offense while combating Rutenberg’s aggressive ways. Brock Bowers’ availability will certainly help Las Vegas, in that regard. The elite tight is hobbled by an ankle injury and his presence is a supreme headache for any and all defensive coordinators. While Mendoza has done an admirable job without his elite pass catcher available, Bowers playing would truly stress Cleveland’s defense and provide an outstanding matchup with the tight end and Schwesinger. Todd Monken knew Brock Bowers was different since Day 1 at Georgia pic.twitter.com/tx5cRmaaqW — Levi Edwards (@theleviedwards) November 24, 2026 Going back to the collective comment from Kubiak at the beginning of this piece, it’ll take the offensive line keeping Mendoza protected, pass catchers separating and getting open from the man-press coverage, and the rookie quarterback smartly distributing the ball. One of the Browns main defensive weaknesses is something the Raiders haven’t done well consistently enough: Running the ball. The aggressive press scheme with single-high safety looks leaves little margin for error against the run and Cleveland is susceptible to the ground and pound allowing 1,263 rushing yards (23rd most amongst the 32 NFL teams). Las Vegas’ run game came to life in Week 11 producing a season-high 143 total rushing yards (previous high was 130 in Week 1). The Silver & Black having that kind of production against the Browns likely goes a long way into determining the team’s success (or lack thereof) this Sunday night. Head-to-Head Sunday night’s clash between the Raiders and Browns marks the 30th meeting between the franchises. The Silver & Black lead the overall series 18-11 (16-11 in regular season play and 2-0 in playoff action) but the Browns won the most recent outing, a 24-10 victory in November of 2025. Before that, however, the Raiders won five-straight meetings dating from 2015 to 2024. That was streak was the second-longest consecutive victories in the overall series by the Raiders. The team won nine-straight from 1974 to 1986 including the postseason clashes in 1981 and 1983. Quotes of Note “Yeah, it’s a really good question. It’s a really fair question. You want to win right now. You want to win every game, but you know that part of the future is those guys having success. So, obviously you go into every game, and you put a game plan together to go win, and you know that some young guys are going to make mistakes. That’s part of their growth. So, that’s just part of it. But you need to give them the reps they need to see it live for us to have success moving forward.” —Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak on balancing the importance of letting younger players develop while also trying to win games “Oh, I’ll tell you, it’s unbelievable, and I believe our rushing offense is on the rise, and those guys work so hard. So, I’m excited to do my 1/11th for the rushing offense, whether it’s carrying out fakes, whether it’s making the right calls or adjustments at the line. I’m just looking forward to keep on doing my 1/11th and getting better at that to help assist the run game.” —Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza on how the run game opened things up for him as a passer

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak spoke to the media ahead of the Week 12 matchup against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday Night Football , informing local reporters that tight end Brock Bowers (ankle) will be questionable for the game. Kubiak also ruled out defensive tackles Adam Butler (concussion), Tonka Hemingway (stinger) and Tim Keenan III (knee), on top of guard/center Jackson Powers-Johnson (Achilles). According to ESPN’s Ryan McFadden , Bowers wasn’t seen on the field during the media viewing period of Friday’s practice. McFadden also noted that the tight end didn’t have his ankle taped on Wednesday but did on Thursday, and that Kubiak didn’t clarify whether Bowers sat out of Friday’s for rest. Kubiak didn’t say whether today was a rest day for Bowers. He added the team has 48 hours to determine if he’s going to suit up. He also didn’t say if Bowers had any setbacks. “We're doing everything we can to get him ready for the game.” Asked the reasoning for Bowers wearing… https://t.co/KiT3wN6J1j — Ryan McFadden (@ryanmcfadden_) November 27, 2026 The two-time Pro Bowler suffered the injury early in the game against the Seattle Seahawks two weeks ago and missed last week’s contest entirely against the Denver Broncos, rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza’s first two starts. That’s forced Mendoza to lean on the Raiders’ other pass-catchers, as running back Ashton Jeanty (nine catches, 136 yards and a touchdown) and wide receiver Jack Bech (10 catches, 98 yards and a touchdown) have been the team’s top receivers during Bowers’ absence. Meanwhile, Butler, Hemingway and Keenan being out leaves Las Vegas with just three healthy defensive tackles (Foley Fatukasi, JJ Pegues and Thomas Booker IV) on the active roster. Veteran Chris Williams was called up from the practice squad last week and played in 24 snaps , collecting a couple of tackles in Denver. Rookie seventh-round pick Brandon Cleveland and veteran Anthony Goodlow are also on the practice squad, while undrafted rookie David Blay Jr. was added to the practice squad this week. At least one, and likely multiple, of those players will be elevated to the active roster for Sunday night to give the Raiders some depth on the defensive line. As for Powers-Johnson, he suffered an Achilles injury during Friday’s practice, and Kubiak said it could be serious, according to McFadden . Powers-Johnson was the Raiders’ starting right guard to begin the season but hasn’t recorded an offensive snap since getting benched after the Week 5 game against the New England Patriots. On the other sideline, the Browns will be without defensive end Derek Barnett (hamstring), while wide receiver Denzel Boston (quad), running back Raheim Sanders (hip) and offensive tackle Austin Barber (knee) are questionable, per The Athletic’s Zac Anderson . #Raiders RG Jackson Powers-Johnson suffered an Achilles injury at practice today. pic.twitter.com/8Epff35fCT — Ryan McFadden (@ryanmcfadden_) November 27, 2026
